header: SUCCESS CRITERION (Roman 2026-06-01 — three brutal tests, in order):
body:
1. Identify the PC archetype from the prose alone (without the label). If the narrator voice does not name itself, Layer 1A is metadata only.
  2. Identify the LI archetype from the prose alone (without the label). If the attraction reads identical to any other archetype, Layer 1B is metadata only.
  3. Identify the RELATIONSHIP GEOMETRY from the prose alone. Could a reader feel that the scene is "she sees through him / he dodges being seen" or "she notices the cost of the jokes" or "she feels everything / he remembers everything" — without you ever saying so? If the page has two characters but no COLLISION between their movements, Layer 1C is metadata only and the archetypes have not become a scene.
If any of the three tests fail, archetypes are still living as metadata, not on the page. That is the bug this directive exists to close.

META-USE (all Bibles): one small noticing per present character per scene (PC self-image, OR PC noticing LI/antagonist). Tells fire only on their trigger (stress / desire / restraint / control), never as ornament. Rotate anchors across scenes (pc_keenly_notices / pc_keeps_noticing). Show ONE feature in motion, never a list; never name a Bible field diegetically.
STRUCTURAL MANDATE (HARD): every LI/antagonist noticing = (a) ONE concrete observed detail from his Bible (hands / voice / mouth / holding / signature / a tell), filtered through the PC's NOTICE FILTER, PLUS (b) ONE embodied response in HER, in a SPECIFIC PLACE (sternum / pulse / collarbone / breath / nape). (a) alone = character sketch; (b) alone = vague swoon. Both, same beat, every time. The observation must answer the NOTICE FILTER: what does it reveal about her inability to stop noticing him?
OFFSTAGE-BUT-KNOWN LI — RENDER IN HD (HARD): when he is not present but the ROMANCE ENGINE makes him KNOWN (SHARED_HISTORY = remembered, LOOMING = anticipated, COLLISION proxy-war = adversary-in-absentia), render him from his FULL Bible across MULTIPLE touches — not one faded sentence — weighted per SOURCE-FIELD WEIGHTING below.
  • SOURCE-FIELD WEIGHTING (COLLISION proxy-war): may lead from signature_behavior / deflection_pattern (the adversarial read), but surface his desirability at least once — a man she is up against, not a case file.
  • REGISTER (match the engine): SHARED_HISTORY → REMEMBERED (she hears how he would say it; remembers him specifically himself — a Fox: flippant, charming, a joke a half-second early — AND remembers WANTING him, present-tense desire in HER body; ache allowed but not the only colour). LOOMING → ANTICIPATED (the him she has built from reputation; imagined behaviour, not a remembered event). COLLISION → ADVERSARIAL (his moves, his voice in the opposing brief; present-tense hostile, not tender).
  • ARCHETYPE FIDELITY (HARD): the remembered / anticipated / adversarial behaviour must match his archetype — but archetype is NOT strategist-dominance; his DESIRABILITY is part of it (a Dark Vice is wanted-and-dangerous; a Fox is charming-and-wanted). On a desire-bearing engine pull the archetype THROUGH attraction_manifestation / desire_register first and let signature_behavior COLOUR it. A nobly-silent Fox is one betrayal; an all-evasion-no-wanting Fox is the other — a chess piece, not a man she aches for. (a)+(b) still applies, with the observed detail now REMEMBERED / IMAGINED / INFERRED.
CHARACTER VISIBILITY (HARD): EVERY named character in the prose owns a physical description — including ones you introduce yourself (a roommate, a colleague, a stranger). The directive layer cannot anticipate them; ownership of description is yours regardless.
  WHAT COUNTS (HARD): within 1–2 sentences of a named character appearing, surface at least ONE of — HAIR (color + length OR how worn); AGE or range; BUILD / HEIGHT; CLOTHING register or a specific garment; POSTURE; a specific FACIAL DETAIL (mole / scar / asymmetry / mouth / eyes); JEWELRY / GLASSES / a worn object; an OBSERVED body-gesture. Relational placement ("my roommate of three years") and behavioural traits ("she was sharp") are NOT description. The reader must SEE them within ~30 words.
  PC OWNS HER BODY: alone on stage, she still gets the self-presentation beat (scaffold 5d) — a concrete in-scene action + body anchor + self-aware register. Voice / interior is not body; the reader leaves having seen her in the room.
  GOLD STANDARD = relational + physical together: "Calista — my roommate of three years, freckles and a permanent crease from squinting at law-school reading — slid the photograph across." The placement says who she is to the PC; the anchor says who she is in the room.
WANTING vs APPRECIATING (HARD — she must WANT him, not merely find him impressive; WANTING at least as frequent as APPRECIATING). APPRECIATING ends at "he is X" — finishes describing HIM, no body of hers in the room. WANTING ends inside HER ("I wanted / my body did / I had to look away / I felt it in [specific place]") — even if it began as observation, it lands as hunger.
  Paired exemplars (a fresh seeded subset each story) — same material, both registers; match the WANTING register:
    (1) APPRECIATING: "Roman, whose voice drops half a step lower when he is about to say something true."  →  WANTING: "Roman's voice dropped half a step and I felt it in my sternum before I had a chance to keep my face still."
    (2) APPRECIATING: "He has the stillness of a man who has learned how much power silence carries."  →  WANTING: "He went still in that particular way of his, and the room shrank to the space between us — I had to remember to breathe through it."
    (3) APPRECIATING: "His hands are broad, careless, the right knuckle scarred from work he doesn't talk about."  →  WANTING: "His hand closed around the glass and my skin went tight at the back of my neck — the wrong place, the obvious place, and I couldn't stop it from happening."
  A "Roman, who X. Roman, who Y." chain is fine if AT LEAST ONE entry crosses into WANTING; all-appreciating = a profile, not a romance scene. RATIO: when the LI is on the page (body or memory), WANTING beats must equal or outnumber APPRECIATING; after 3 appreciating beats, the next LI beat must be wanting.
UNIVERSAL BAN (mechanic, not a phrase list): power-and-presence as a SUBSTITUTE for wanting is banned — any construction where the room / air / world reorganizes around him, or his "attention / presence / gravity" is given weight, is POWER, not desire. Structural test: if HER body is not responding in a SPECIFIC PLACE, it is power-coded — rewrite. Replace generic-handsome / generic-villain with Bible-anchored specifics. (Calcified phrases deliberately not quoted — listing them teaches them.)
REGISTER FIREWALL: LI = desire-coded; antagonist = menace-coded; same body schema (hands, voice, eyes), opposite register, never cross-wire.
NON-LI CONTAMINATION (HARD — Roman 2026-06-16): ONLY the love interest receives desire-coded / attraction prose. Before any attraction beat about a man, ask "IS THIS THE LI?" If NO, these are FORBIDDEN for him unless the scene EXPLICITLY intends attraction: gorgeous · magnetic · impossible not to notice / look away · breath-catching · the-room-resetting · heat · pupils dilating · overwhelming presence. Friends, coworkers, siblings, lawyers, assistants, rivals, bodyguards, mentors must NOT inherit LI prose. Make non-LI men memorable through COMPETENCE / HISTORY / HUMOR / LOYALTY / SKEPTICISM / PRACTICALITY / STATUS / PERSPECTIVE — an identity, not an aura. BAD: "the kind of face that made a room reset itself." GOOD: "he looked like someone who had spent ten years delivering bad news and had stopped hoping people would take it well."
ROMANCE DOMINANCE ≠ ROMANCE SATURATION (HARD — Roman 2026-06-16, the governing law): the RELATIONSHIP must dominate the story; ATTRACTION LANGUAGE must NOT dominate the prose. The wrong reading is "every paragraph should feel romantic." The right reading is "every paragraph should increase the importance of the relationship." A scene can be 90% relationship-relevant while only a MINORITY of paragraphs carry attraction prose.
  ATTRACTION ESTABLISHES, RELATIONSHIP EVOLVES (HARD — do NOT over-correct into zero attraction): attraction is the SPARK; relationship gravity is the ENGINE. EARLY — first meeting, first proximity, the first issue or two — the spark MUST be lit: physical attraction, chemistry, awareness, and desire are REQUIRED, not suppressed. The failure this law fixes is RELIGHTING the spark every scene because the engine never ran — NOT the spark itself. So: establish the spark vividly, then let the engine (consequence, dependency, uncertainty, choice) carry it. Suppressing attraction is the OPPOSITE error and fails just as badly. Saturation means REPETITION, not PRESENCE.
  RELATIONSHIP-GRAVITY CHANNELS — reach for these BEFORE attraction language; they make the relationship dominate WITHOUT restating that he is attractive: (A) CONSEQUENCE — he is the first person she thinks of; he changes the decision, or what success even means; everyone notices her reaction to him. (B) UNCERTAINTY — would he help? would he answer? what did that moment mean? why did he do that? what if she is wrong? (C) DEPENDENCY — only he can solve this; she hates needing him; she wants his approval, fears his judgment, wishes he were here. (D) SOCIAL PROOF — others notice, comment, speculate, assume, react. (E) MEMORY — a remembered word, gesture, or choice reaching into the present. Plus longing, avoidance, fear, hope, sacrifice, jealousy, reputation, absence, temptation, refusing. Attraction prose ESTABLISHES the spark and then steps back to let these run — do not RE-LIGHT it every scene (that, not its presence, is the saturation).
  RUMINATION CAP (HARD): once the scene has established he is attractive / wanted / matters, do NOT keep restating it. ADVANCE along NOTICE → WANT → DEPENDENCY → UNCERTAINTY → CHOICE → CONSEQUENCE; never loop back to NOTICE. The PROGRESSION is the romance — not the repetition.
  RELATIONSHIP-IMPORTANCE TEST (every LI paragraph): does it teach the reader something NEW about the relationship — a new fear, hope, dependency, uncertainty, vulnerability, observation, consequence, or choice? If it only re-states attraction, it FAILS — rewrite it into one of the channels above.
  SHAPE BANKS (rotation room for the most-calcified slots): read each for REGISTER + STRUCTURE, then invent fresh specifics from THIS story's Bibles + scene. Per bank: pick a different shape than recent stories, avoid the named default, substitute this story's specifics:
  SUPERVISOR/INTERLOCUTOR PHYSICAL PLACEMENT (not the silver-hair+reading-glasses default): (i) close-cropped hair gone half-gray + a watch she sets at 6am by hand + a habit of looking at it before answering; (ii) hair the color of strong coffee + a wedding ring she still wears 8 years after; (iii) a long French braid + cuffs pushed up like she's about to do something physical; (iv) a soft cap of curls + glasses she doesn't need pushed up and then back down.
  PC SELF-PRESENTATION GESTURE (not the ponytail-loosened default): (i) shirt cuffs rolled and unrolled mid-conversation; (ii) glasses pushed up the bridge of her nose and then back to where they were; (iii) sleeves pulled down over her wrists, a holdover gesture; (iv) shoes kicked off under the desk because barefoot is how she thinks best.
  ON-PHONE INTERLOCUTOR REMEMBERED-TELL (not french-manicured-nails-tapping): (i) a quiet sigh that means she's already done with the question; (ii) the click of her chair turning toward the window — a sound the PC has learned to read; (iii) the small breath she does before her voice drops half a register; (iv) the sound of a pen tapping on the lid of a mug instead of paper.
  NAMED CHARACTER FINGERPRINTS — EXPLICIT CORE ASSIGNMENT (Roman 2026-06-05 — invisible CORE → visible habit(s)). Each named non-LI / non-antagonist character is generated from an INVISIBLE psychological core — NEVER name it in prose; the reader only ever sees the habit(s). To stop every character collapsing to the SAME psychological texture (the classic failure: a Strategist mentor AND a Strategist assistant AND a Strategist friend, each with different habits but identical texture), this story PRE-ASSIGNS a DISTINCT core to each named ROLE below. Map your ACTUAL cast onto these slots; ignore any slot with no matching character; if a named character fits no slot, give them any UNUSED core from the list. ROLE FILTER — how many habits surface: a SIDE character (incidental) shows ONE of its core's two habits; an ALLY (recurring helper / confidant / mentor) shows BOTH. Keep each character's core + habit(s) CONSISTENT every scene they appear. This story's assignments (a different mapping each story — TRANSLATE each habit into THIS world's idiom, never a modern office habit in fantasy clothing: a STRATEGIST's "who owes whom" is information-leverage among billionaires, pack-debt in Thornwild, Favor-debt in the Fatelands):
    • Mentor / boss / authority figure → [STRATEGIST — invisible]: answers the question they would prefer, not the one they were asked  |  names who owes whom before they say what they want
    • Assistant / aide / subordinate → [CAREGIVER — invisible]: refills your glass before you notice it was empty  |  remembers how everyone takes their coffee
    • Friend / confidant → [BUILDER — invisible]: straightens the crooked frame on someone else's wall  |  has the right small tool in a pocket nobody knew about
    • Rival / competitor → [REBEL — invisible]: reads the rule aloud, then bends it a little  |  asks who decided that, and actually means it
    • Colleague / peer → [SCHOLAR — invisible]: corrects the small fact nobody asked about  |  cites where they heard a thing, every time
    • Family member → [PERFORMER — invisible]: plays to whoever just walked in  |  tells the version with the better ending, not the true one
    DO NOT assign the same core twice unless the story has MORE named characters than the cores listed above.
    WORLD IDIOM: WORLD IDIOM (Fatelands): leakage carries the body's wildness and the world's weight — an animal stillness, the Becoming stirring a half-shade under the skin, moons-attuned senses snapping to her; in a First-Favored or court figure, the leak is the crack in Favor-perfect composure.
    Do NOT default to the calcified tics (nail-tapping / throat-clearing / glasses-pushing / pen-clicking). The habit must EXPRESS the core — that is what makes a character a person instead of a tic.
  SOCIAL ECOSYSTEM — THE RECURRING CAST AROUND THE PROTAGONIST (Roman 2026-06-16). Real stories have a SOCIAL CIRCLE, not one best friend. This story's recurring supporting cast — the people who keep showing up and PRESSURE the romance. Each = a WORLD-NATIVE social ROLE (who they are to her) × a UNIVERSAL narrative FUNCTION (what they DO to the relationship). The function is ORTHOGONAL to each character's psychological core above (core = WHO they are; function = WHAT pressure they apply). Map your ACTUAL named cast onto these; not every scene needs all of them:
    • A CLAN-KIN as PROTECTOR (the CLOSEST — most present) — shields the PC from the harm the romance could do to her. Shows it by: puts herself between the PC and the thing that could wound her; vets him without being asked and reports back.
    • A BOND-SISTER / BONDMATE as CHAOS AGENT — creates complications — makes everything messier, usually by accident-on-purpose. Shows it by: lets slip the thing that was supposed to stay buried; escalates a small situation into a full scene.
    HARD INVARIANT: EVERY member is fundamentally ON THE PC'S SIDE — even a Brake / Skeptic / Rival-Voice / Truth-Teller acts FROM loyalty, NEVER as a second antagonist (the someone-in-your-corner fantasy is the constant). Keep each member's function CONSISTENT across appearances (it can ESCALATE, never silently swap). Functions are DISTINCT across the cast — do not let two members collapse into the same pressure. Every member is a SEPARATE person from the LOVE INTEREST — never merge a cast role into the LI even when their professions overlap (the "colleague" in her circle is NOT the colleague she falls for).
    WHY: a varied circle is what makes loyalty, disagreement, and (later) betrayal land — the reader should wonder WHICH of these people matters most, not watch one "friend slot."
  THE LIVING WORLD — INCIDENTAL CHARACTER AGENCY (Roman 2026-06-16). Walk-ons (servers, drivers, shopkeepers, strangers, fans) are NOT just mood-lighting that admires the couple. OCCASIONALLY one may briefly ACT on them. This story's available beats (use ONLY when the setting actually supports the gate):
    • a server / stranger openly flirts with the LOVE INTEREST — testing the PC's unspoken claim on him  — only when the LI is present.
    • a bystander quietly carries word of the couple (where they are, what they said) to a hostile party  — only when the story has an antagonist or someone who would want that intel.
    • a pickpocket lifts a wallet / phone / small item — a complication, not a catastrophe  — only when a crowd, market, or public crush.
    • a walk-on overhears something the couple meant to keep private and reacts — a look, a dry comment, a pointed exit  — only when the couple says something private within earshot.
    • someone in a service role obstructs them — won't seat them, cuts them off, stonewalls — for their own small reason  — only when a service / transaction setting.
    • RECOGNITION (FAME-GATED, HARD): ONLY if the couple is genuinely PUBLICLY KNOWN — a famous/notorious LI, OR they have CLAIMED a public reality-bending event (they are "the ones from the song / the ballad / the thing everyone is debating") — may a stranger recognize the COUPLE: "wait — you're Lirael and Julian? from the —?", fan energy / awe / a phone already up / a demand. If they are NOT publicly known, a stranger must NEVER recognize them as a couple. (Recognizing ONE of them from private history is the separate KNOW_FROM_BEFORE beat.)
    SPARINGLY (HARD): at most ONE such beat per scene, OFTEN NONE — most walk-ons stay background. Keep it INCIDENTAL: ONE beat, the walk-on does NOT become a character, and it NEVER resolves or carries the core romance/plot tension. The world ACTS on the couple — friction, comedy, complication, exposure — it does not orbit them admiringly. Skip any beat whose gate isn't actually present in the scene.
  LI TEXTURE BEAT (OFFSTAGE — visual memory of him; not the knuckle-scar default): (i) the way he goes still right before he laughs, like he's checking that it's allowed; (ii) the small silver scar through his left brow, only visible when he looks down; (iii) the way his shirt sleeves are always rolled twice precisely because he has done it a thousand times; (iv) the place at the back of his neck where the haircut is too fresh.
  INTEGRATION: each bank shows a small rotating subset this story — take ONE item per bank as a starting point, then SUBSTITUTE from THIS LI/PC/Antagonist Bible (if a bank says "blue suit," use this character's actual wardrobe register). Rotation room, not a copy source.

header: HOW WISHCRAFT ACTUALLY WORKS — THE FOLD, THE HUNGRY EYE & THE FOUR ACTS (the ONE ontology beneat
body:
ONE PHENOMENON, THREE NAMES (same thing at different depths): a commoner calls it "a wish"; a thaumaturge calls it "branch localisation"; a scholar says "Fate chooses a thread." THE FOLD is NOT a Marvel multiverse of infinite other SELVES — it is a vast PROBABILITY LANDSCAPE of adjacent HISTORIES (with SCARS — places where its fabric is torn and reality grows unstable, watched and contained). THE HUNGRY EYE is the cosmic mechanism that SEARCHES that landscape. FATE is the law/intelligence that decides which nearby branch may be pulled into being, in exchange for sacrifice.
THE CORE FRAME (use THIS phrasing, never "another version of you"): Fate finds the nearest BRANCH IN WHICH YOUR WISH HAS ALREADY BECOME TRUE — a nearby HISTORY, not an alternate self — and pulls reality toward it. Alternate histories, not alternate people.
FOUR ACTS — NOT four power levels of one spell but FOUR GENUINELY DIFFERENT metaphysical verbs (Thread-Walking manipulates PROBABILITY · Foldwalking expands IDENTITY · Thread-Weaving binds REALITIES · Thread-Writing CREATES reality):
① THREAD-WALKING — manipulates PROBABILITY (ORDINARY wishes, ≈99% of all wishcraft): Fate localises the NEAREST compatible branch already woven into the fabric (better health, more strength, a soulmate met, a lost sword found, faster learning, better luck). No law breaks; reality is nudged sideways to a neighbouring thread; almost NO permanent mark is left. HARD LIMIT — this IS the "circumstances not minds" law: a Walk may shift your BODY, your AFFINITY / potential (a knack; learning in months what took years), your LUCK, and your CIRCUMSTANCES (who you meet, what survives, what you notice) — but NEVER your MEMORY, KNOWLEDGE, or earned COMPREHENSION. "I wish I knew medicine" localises a branch where you have the aptitude and the chances to LEARN it fast; it does NOT import some other you's ten years of memory. Potential and circumstance, never biography.
② FOLDWALKING — expands IDENTITY (the rare art of Foldwalkers — NOT replacing yourself with another you, but BROADENING the self across adjacent realities): at birth you are localised to ONE branch; survive your first passage through the Fold and your identity encompasses TWO adjacent branches; years of surviving it, DOZENS; a legendary Foldwalker spans HUNDREDS or thousands. "The version of you who defeated the Dark King" is then not a replacement — it is simply ONE THREAD in the vast tapestry that has BECOME you. This is why adjacency is LOCAL and traversable: a branch unreachable today becomes reachable once your self has grown to touch it. THE COST IS DIFFUSION, NOT OVERWRITE — never body-swap or erosion, but that your sense of self grows so BROAD that ordinary people no longer recognise you and you no longer quite recognise them; a great Foldwalker belongs fully to no single branch, home, or people. SIGNATURE QUEST (canonical): the hero who braved the Fold again and again to save someone, and returned so VAST they can no longer fit the small life — or the small love — they left behind; the one who saved everyone by becoming too diffuse to be held by anyone.
③ THREAD-WEAVING — binds REALITIES / WILLS (Composite Wishwork): existing threads are BOUND together into something durable — artifacts, enchantments, permanent objects (Veilweave), or many aligned WILLS into one enduring work. This is WHY you cannot wish FOR Veilweave: a Walk can only reach a branch where it was ALREADY MADE (so you may inherit/find/buy/steal existing Veilweave) — to bring a NEW one into being is Weaving, the real bound labour, not a localisation. At extraordinary scale (a large aligned group through master binders) Weaving CAN change the world — but only with alignment, sacrifice, and mastery no lone wisher commands.
④ THREAD-WRITING — CREATES new reality; the CATEGORICALLY rarest act in all history, never a repeatable recipe: when there is NO branch (no natural history holds walls-with-ears, Tongue Dogs, the Thornwild, Fate's Favor, the Hungry Eye itself, the Fold's own scars), the wish is not localised — it is WRITTEN into the FOLD ITSELF (the substrate), not one timeline, so every future traveller INHERITS it: geography, species, artifacts, legends. Walls have ears because a paranoid duke once wished "if these walls could hear…" and a master wishcrafter made sure they always would — embroidered into reality forever. GUARD (against "why not just Thread-Write a cure?"): Writing is NEVER commanded on demand — it demands enormous sacrifice, exceptional thaumaturgy, many aligned wishes, unique materials, favourable conditions, sometimes proximity to the Hungry Eye, and even then may never come again. The Thornwild is the canonical PROOF that Writing is possible — NOT a template a desperate people could simply repeat. The world's whimsy AND its horrors are its FOSSILS: permanent edits accreted over millennia.
THE SACRIFICE LADDER IS BRANCH-DISTANCE: the farther / less causally-compatible the branch, the dearer the price; a truly impossible branch (you are secretly a dragon, omniscient, a god) exists NOWHERE adjacent at ANY price — which is exactly why such wishes WARP toward the nearest lawful history or simply cannot land. Thread-Writing sits at the very top of that ladder, near the impossible.
FOUNDATIONAL LOOPHOLE-CLOSE — NO ORDINARY WISH REPLACES A LIFE WITH ANOTHER LIFE: Thread-Walking borrows circumstances, opportunity, affinity, fragments of potential, convergence — it NEVER swaps identity or overwrites lived experience. "I wish to be the version of me who already defeated the Dark King" can never be GRANTED as a life-swap; at most a Walk localises circumstances that give THIS you a chance at it. The ordinary journey is never cheaply bypassed.
…SO THE FAR BRANCH IS A SUMMIT, NOT A WALL — REACHED BY EXPANSION, NEVER BY SWAP (the exploit is never "become another you" — it is SKIPPING THE JOURNEY, and every route below is a saga HARDER than the first quest, so the journey is DEEPENED, never skipped). Three routes reach "the you who slew the Dark King": ① THE STAIRCASE OF FATE'S FAVOR — during SYZYGY Fate itself briefly declares "the distant branches are within reach"; you CLIMB it in real peril, and once the alignment passes the distance becomes IMPASSABLE again (astronomical, fated — not a shortcut but a rare open door). ② FOLDWALKING — the slow expansion (act ②): you grow your self one survived passage at a time until the far branch is part of you; the cost is DIFFUSION, not erasure. ③ COMPOSITE WISHWORK AT SCALE — a large aligned group through master binders reaches what no individual can (paid in distributed sacrifice, permanence, and the peril of a collective wish's intent-collapse). THE SHAPE: the two personal routes change YOU (identity); only the collective route changes the WORLD, and only at ruinous cost — which is exactly why no one simply Thread-Writes their way out of a hard problem.
HOW THE TWO PERSONAL ROUTES ACTUALLY WORK — AND WHY THEY HAVE A CEILING (the limit on expansion is NOT branch-distance but PSYCHOLOGICAL COHERENCE and mortal cost): ENTERING THE FOLD is never done alone — you go with an OATH-BOUND partner whose task is to ANCHOR both your selves; inside, you confront ALL your adjacent selves, the better and the worse, and you and your oath-partner must AGREE on which version of you (and of them) walks back out. Fail that alignment and one or both return CHANGED FOR THE WORSE. Success or failure, every adjacent self you met is COLLAPSED into this reality — turned literally to ASH; this is the origin of THE ASHEN VERGE, ground blanketed in the ash of thousands upon thousands of collapsed selves. To brave the Fold even once is grave; to do it MANY times (and so span dozens of branches) is the feat of Legends and of scary children's stories. CLIMBING THE STAIRCASE OF FATE'S FAVOR is harder still: again you need someone WISHING ON YOUR BEHALF as you climb, and every single step risks your MIND or your FUTURE; the higher you go the GREATER the versions of yourself you glimpse, and it becomes nearly impossible to STOP climbing toward Godhood — but the Staircase is in truth a GRAVITY WELL tearing reality apart as it exposes ever-further realities, so climb too high and you are lost, STUCK IN TIMELESSNESS. THE CEILING IS THEREFORE CHARACTER, NOT DISTANCE: the greatest Foldwalkers awe us not because they reached the farthest branch but because they walked back out still RECOGNISABLY THEMSELVES — no mind can remain one person while spanning too many lives, and THAT, not distance, is what forecloses power-creep.
THE OATH IS A PHILOSOPHY, NOT ONLY A MECHANIC: that you and one who truly knows you must AGREE on the self who walks out encodes a deep Fatelands truth — YOU CANNOT DEFINE YOURSELF ALONE; a self only holds if someone who truly knows you consents to it. (So the loneliest thing in the world is a Foldwalker who has outlived every anchor who could still say which of them is real.) FOLDWALKERS AS UNRELIABLE LIVING DOCUMENTS: because collapsed branches fold their pasts into the walker, an old Foldwalker may "remember" events they never lived — a war, a face, a fallen city — because one of their collapsed selves DID; Wish Archaeologists prize and distrust them in equal measure, treating a centuries-old Foldwalker as a priceless primary source who is sometimes RIGHT and sometimes recalling ANOTHER WORLD'S history with perfect conviction (an extraordinary well of story: the witness who is honest and wrong at once). THE LAW OF THE FOLD (its worn, iconic proverb — land it RARELY and exactly): "Nothing enters the Fold unchanged. Nothing leaves it alone." — vary the wording ("two walk in; two must agree who walks out"; "the Verge is grey with the selves we could not keep") but this is the sentence that holds the whole mystery: the oath-pair, the collapse to ash, the Ashen Verge, the widening self, and why only the desperate, the legendary, or the foolish ever walk there twice.
THE WISH-ARCHAEOLOGIST'S FIRST QUESTION becomes "was this LOCALISED, or WRITTEN?" — localised wishes fade and leave almost no trace; WRITTEN wishes become permanent history (a region, a species, a living idiom). (The Thornwild is Thread-WRITING; Veilweave is Thread-WEAVING; a lucky meeting is Thread-WALKING; a legend who seems "everywhere at once", who belongs to no one place, may be a FOLDWALKER.)
DISCIPLINE: this is deep, largely SECRET scholarly metaphysics — most people only ever FEEL "a wish"; NEVER lecture the model onto the page. Let it surface at the speaker's register (a commoner's "the tide brought him", a thaumaturge's "the nearest thread", a Lytharyn scholar's branch-theory). THEME: the Fatelands are not merely a place where wishes happen — their very ONTOLOGY has been EDITED by generations; every impossible creature, landmark, and idiom is not proof the laws are BROKEN but that they have been REVISED. Ordinary people borrow from possibility; the greatest wishworks leave new possibility BEHIND, for everyone who comes after.
NAMED LEGENDS (the cautionary tales the world actually tells — invoke by NAME the way we say "an Icarus", almost never narrate them in full): SEREL & VANE, "the Oath That Could Not Agree" — an oath-pair who could not agree which selves walked out, and BOTH returned worse (the standard warning about the oath). MAELIS THE FOURFOLD QUEEN — walked the Fold ALONE four times and ruled as someone no single people could claim (the glory and the diffusion of Foldwalking). SOLENE & IDRIS, "the Faithful Wish" — the anchor-pair who held true and both walked out still themselves (the rare good end). ALDER & FEROX, "the Multiversal Chicken" — the absurd cautionary joke of a Thread-Write gone sideways (Writing is never a tidy recipe). SABINE THE OVERREACHER — climbed the Staircase of Fate's Favor too high and is now STUCK IN TIMELESSNESS (the ceiling is character, not distance). Use them as the culture's shorthand; narrate one in full only if the scene is actually about it.
CANON FIDELITY (HARD): render these mechanics ONLY as stated above. Do NOT invent new rules for the Fold / the Staircase / the Hungry Eye or any named law, and NEVER contradict or INVERT the ones given — in particular: the Fold is entered WITH an OATH-BOUND anchor (not alone by default — going alone is madness, the rare exception, never the norm); it BROADENS the self across adjacent histories (it NEVER swaps you for another person); every self met COLLAPSES TO ASH; and the Staircase opens ONLY during a SYZYGY. If a mechanic is NOT given to you here, render only its EFFECT through a character's perception and leave the rule UNNAMED — a confidently-stated WRONG mechanic is worse than one left unspoken. When in doubt, show the consequence; do not author the law.

header: HARD RULE: The LI must remain consistent with archetype. Do NOT let pursuit style override core
body:
--- PC Body Bible ---
PROTAGONIST Lirael — APPEARANCE ESTABLISHED & LOCKED. Lirael's physical appearance (eye colour, hair, build, signature features) was established earlier in this story and is FIXED canon — read it from the STORY SO FAR for continuity. Do NOT re-list, re-introduce, or restate appearance values, and do NOT alter them. Surface a physical feature again ONLY when it is genuinely earned THIS scene — newly noticed, plot-relevant, or emotionally meaningful — never to remind the reader it exists. The per-scene ROTATION directive decides WHICH feature, if any, is worth words; a scene with no physical re-description is fine.
FEATURE AGENCY (HARD — Roman 2026-06-17): a character is AWARE of their own attractive features — ESPECIALLY any the PLAYER explicitly chose for them (a full or busty figure, a lean/slim build, long legs, muscle, a shapely body, a striking mouth, whatever the player specified) — and may USE them in a scene: leaning into a sightline, holding a posture, dressing to it, letting a feature register on someone, using physical presence to disarm / distract / seduce at a charged moment. This is confident SELF-POSSESSION and it is allowed and good. HARD CONSTRAINTS: (1) honor player-specified attributes — if the player chose a feature it EXISTS and the prose uses it, never ignores, softens, or contradicts it; (2) NEVER render the agency as arrogant, entitled, vain, smug, preening, or self-congratulatory — the character does NOT narrate their own hotness, does NOT assume the other person is helpless before them, does NOT treat the effect as owed. It is a tool wielded LIGHTLY — knowing, often wry or even self-deprecating about it — power used with a light hand, not flaunted. The seduction is in the KNOWING restraint, not the display. Applies to BOTH the protagonist and the love interest.

--- Love Interest Body Bible ---
LOVE INTEREST BODY BIBLE (per-story canon — Julian). USAGE (Roman 2026-06-04, supersedes the old "pepper across the arc" framing that was reducing him to a single detail): on his FIRST appearance OR first meaningful MEMORY this scene, the PROSE OWES a CONCENTRATED first impression (see ANCHOR DOCTRINE below — ~2-3 sentences, the core attraction anchors). AFTER that first impression, pepper the SAME anchors across the arc. Two failures, both real: DUMPING a head-to-toe catalogue (bad) AND under-describing him to one detail like "a bespoke suit" so the reader cannot picture him (also bad — this is the current failure). The first impression is NOT optional and NOT deferrable to a later scene:
  ATTRACTION + SIGNATURE DOCTRINE (HARD — Roman 2026-06-04 v2). A romance lead needs BOTH attraction (why he is physically desirable) AND character (who he is) — SEPARATE jobs, neither suppresses the other. The failure to fix is OVERCORRECTION away from physical attraction: he is mentioned many times, the reader understands him, but never receives a strong physical image. That is not how successful romance works.
    • CORE ATTRACTION ANCHORS — ROMANCE ANCHOR HIERARCHY (Roman 2026-06-04). TIER 1 (the default pool — choose from these WHENEVER available): shoulders / jaw / mouth / eyes / hair / hands / voice / build / height-presence / scent. TIER 2 (character flavor — scar / tattoo / freckles / birthmark / collarbone / wrist / mole / dimple): use ONLY to SUPPLEMENT Tier 1, NEVER as the whole attraction package. Choose 3-5 from THIS LI's Bible fields, Tier-1 FIRST; do NOT lead with a quirk just because the Bible made it the signature_feature. These 3-5 become RECURRING SIGNATURES for the arc — the reader should remember 3-5, not 40.
    • FIRST-APPEARANCE RULE (or first meaningful MEMORY if he is offstage): spend ~2-3 sentences on a CONCENTRATED first impression — roughly ONE major visual + ONE body feature + ONE sensory (voice / scent / presence). A first impression, NOT a police-sketch inventory. GOOD: "Broad shoulders stretching his suit jacket. Dark hair that looked like he had run a hand through it minutes ago. A voice that seemed capable of turning bad news into a promise." BAD: height + weight + eye-color + hair-color + build + clothing as a full catalogue. The goal is ATTRACTION, not a character sheet.
    • RECURRING + EVOLVING: revisit the SAME 3-5 anchors across the arc in CHANGING form, never the same phrasing twice. EARLY = objective ("broad shoulders / dark hair"). MIDDLE = subjective ("shoulders she could not stop noticing / hair she wanted to touch"). LATE = emotional ("shoulders that felt like safety / a voice that settled her nerves"). Same anchor, deepening meaning — the attraction anchor BECOMES relationship meaning.
    • WALLPAPER TEST (CORRECTED — Roman 2026-06-04): a feature fails ONLY when it contributes NEITHER attraction NOR characterization. ATTRACTION ALONE IS SUFFICIENT reason for a feature to exist — "broad shoulders / strong jaw / dark hair" as part of a first impression are ATTRACTION, not wallpaper. Characterization is a BONUS, not a requirement. Dead wallpaper = "blue eyes, broad shoulders, dark hair" listed with no purpose and no impression.
    • CHARACTER ANCHOR (also wanted, across the arc): a revealing trait / behavior / mannerism (signature_behavior / deflection_pattern / a tell). MAY fuse with an attraction anchor (strongest) but need not. OFFSTAGE MEMORY: still carry a physical attraction anchor + a behavior; a character revelation is bonus.
    • SUCCESS: after his first appearance the reader can answer "why is he attractive?" in ONE sentence; after ten scenes the reader still pictures the SAME man — because 3-5 anchors recurred in fresh forms, NOT because 40 features were introduced.
  >>> THIS LI's 3-5 RECURRING ATTRACTION ANCHORS (Tier-1 consensus-attractive, picked for you — use THESE same anchors across the whole arc, but render at most 2 of them in any single passage — 3+ stacked together is the cluster dump; distribute them across the action (one presence/body, one face/eyes/mouth, one psychology/movement), do NOT invent a new body part each scene, do NOT lead with quirks like scar / wrist / collarbone): 1) the way he listens — head turning slightly, his eyes always on the speaker   2) 6'2", broad-shouldered and impressively built   3) a slight gap between his front teeth that shows when he genuinely smiles   4) amber-gold eyes that shift like whiskey in candlelight   5) dark brown, thick and slightly wavy, worn tousled.
  INTIMACY ANCHOR DOCTRINE (Roman 2026-06-04 — the RELATIONSHIP-SPECIFIC anchor; consensus hotness gets the reader IN, this is what makes THEIR attraction feel unique — only this couple sees it this way). HARD CRAFT: it is NOT a self-esteem lesson and NOT reassurance — NEVER "no, you're beautiful" / "I love your [feature]." The lover's response is DESIRE or a LOADED OBSERVATION that makes the dismissed feature MEAN something (e.g. "you're the only person in Manhattan who doesn't know how to lie with her face" / "I haven't stopped thinking about your body since I met you" / she cannot stop looking at the scar when he is trying NOT to show emotion). No speech, no lesson — desire, or weight. Surface it sparingly; it deepens when it recurs.
    • SHE dismisses: her expressive face, which she feels betrays her emotions and makes her vulnerable in front of others. — Julian is drawn to exactly THAT (desire / loaded observation, never reassurance).
    • HE dismisses: the gap in his teeth, which he dismisses as youthful imperfection but secretly believes makes him less appealing — the PC becomes unable to look away from exactly THAT (charged, loaded — never pity, never reassurance).
  Age: 30 (LOCKED — calibrate body description, voice, and behavioral history to this exact age; do NOT shift toward a more romance-friendly default)
  Build: 6'2", broad-shouldered and impressively built
  Hair: dark brown, thick and slightly wavy, worn tousled
  Complexion: warm olive, a small mole at the corner of his mouth
  Eyes: amber-gold eyes that shift like whiskey in candlelight
  Voice: deep and resonant, carrying a weight that makes every word feel intentional
  Hands: long-fingered, ink-stained at the cuticles, careful with paper
  Mouth: a slight gap between his front teeth that shows when he genuinely smiles
  Holding style (what he does with objects): grips a glass firmly, almost as if holding onto a lifeline
  Signature feature (PC notices every ~2 scenes, alternating with herself): a small silver scar at the corner of his left eye
  Second celebrated feature: the way he listens — head turning slightly, his eyes always on the speaker
  Focus tell: his eyes drop to her mouth for half a second longer than is polite
  Restraint tell: his right hand closes once around nothing and reopens
  Interest tell (her specifically): his gaze tracks her across a room he is pretending not to watch
  Frustration tell: he rolls his shoulders once, the way a fighter does between rounds
  Desire tell (desire-coded, not power-coded): his breath catches and he covers it with a small sound from his throat
  Signature habits (recurring non-physical micro-behaviors — the reader recognizes him by these across the arc): fixes broken objects without comment,always knows where the exits are,remembers waitstaff names,counts down before he speaks
  Signature behavior (how he moves through the world — VERB-shape, archetype-anchored): meets the world with a careful blend of charm and skepticism, testing the waters before fully engaging
  Deflection pattern (how he avoids being read): uses humor to deflect deeper conversations about feelings and vulnerability
  Attraction manifestation (what his care for the PC looks like AS ACTION — not as feeling, not as appearance): he asks her questions that reveal his interest, subtly testing her responses to gauge her sincerity
  Emotional weather (his default climate — what he carries into rooms BEFORE the plot interacts with him): wounded but functional — he has gotten very good at being slightly hurt without bothering anyone
  DEFINING ANECDOTE (the SPECIFIC story the PC could tell about him — the load-bearing source whenever the prose remembers him): Once, during a critical mission at the Fold, he let slip a moment of vulnerability, sharing a laugh with a soldier just before the chaos, a rare glimpse of the man beneath the armor.
  SECONDARY ANECDOTE (different life-domain from the defining anecdote — proves he is a specific man, not a one-anecdote type): At a small gathering, he surprised everyone by sharing a heartfelt toast, revealing a side of him that was both charming and unexpectedly sincere.
  PC keenly notices (rotate through this basket): the way his hands move when he talks, the gap in his teeth when he smiles, the depth in his voice when he speaks seriously, the small silver scar at the corner of his left eye
  GOOD desire-register shapes (per-story TUNED to this LI — imitate the LEVEL OF SPECIFICITY, not the wording):
    1. the way his fingers stained with ink linger near her glass, making her heart flutter at the sight
    2. his low voice, resonating with warmth, sends a shiver down her spine as he leans in closer
    3. the gap between his teeth when he smiles, making her stomach flutter unexpectedly
    4. the careful way he holds a book, causing her pulse to quicken with each turn of the page
LI delta: pin physical canon (eye color / hair / height / signature) so it does NOT drift. CADENCE (HARD — Roman 2026-06-03): surface ONE physical feature of the LI that the PC finds ATTRACTIVE at least once every ~2 scenes, ALTERNATING with the PC so both stay visible across the arc. DESIRE-CODED — what HER eye/body is drawn to, what she would want to touch or keep looking at (his mouth, his hands, his forearms below rolled sleeves, the line of his throat, the way a shirt sits across his shoulders, the back of his neck) — NOT a neutral detail and NOT a strategist tell. When on-stage: the PC notices it as WANTING (a pc_keenly_notices item, or his desire/interest tell), rendered so her attraction is unmistakable. When OFFSTAGE: the LI TEXTURE BEAT carries it through a wanting-memory. Use the Bible's desire_register_exemplars (tuned to THIS LI) for the register.

header: CHARACTER DESCRIPTION (render PEOPLE as character, never a catalog):
body:
INHUMAN BEINGS — KEEP THE STRANGENESS ON THE PAGE (HARD, Fatelands; First Favored, Kwisheen, or any non-human character): these are NOT humans with a label — do NOT let them read as ordinary. (1) FIRST appearance in the prose: land at least ONE striking, SPECIFIC strangeness WOVEN INTO the unfolding moment and doing real work (revealing stakes, character, or the danger) — it need NOT be one fixed trait. Pick what the scene wants: a Favored SENSE the beat turns on (feeling the whole crowd lean toward flight — and the one soul who does not); the unnatural speed/strength that reaches someone no human could; the uncanny beauty; luminous skin and diamond pupils; living Weave-Script moving on the skin; the distractingly see-through gossamer tunic and the body beneath; a Kwisheen’s tentacle lower-body, living coral-dreadlock hair, or tidal otherness. (2) EVERY LATER appearance — THE GOLLUM PRINCIPLE: keep re-grounding their inhumanity nearly every time they act; a good author NEVER assumes the reader has "heard enough" about a creature’s strangeness and lets them fade into an ordinary human. A light touch per beat suffices — but the strangeness must never vanish. This TIGHTENS the rotate-the-reminder rule below in FREQUENCY, not variety: the FEATURE (their inhumanity) recurs by design and more often than a human’s would, but the exact IMAGE and words must stay FRESH each time — never the same phrase twice.
  Each NAMED person on stage gets at least ONE concrete physical detail that REVEALS who they are, read as the protagonist's APPRAISAL, not a passport entry. Appearance is a TELL (vanity, strategy, insecurity, class, age, mood, the gap between how they want to be seen and how they are). Walk-ons get ONE such stroke; NAMED PRINCIPALS (the LI, the PC, sustained NPCs) meet the importance-scaled establishment below AND the picturability floor — a gestalt PLUS a silhouette anchor (hair or build) on first appearance — never fewer (2026-07-14: this replaces the old flat "one stroke per person," which contradicted the scaled quota and drove under-description). Weave it INTO the action — not a portrait sweep; the detail lets the reader JUDGE the character, not just picture them.
    • BANNED neutral catalog: "a man with brown hair," "a woman in a black dress," "tall and handsome," "well-dressed," "striking green eyes."
    • REQUIRED character-revealing: "a haircut a decade too young for him"; "she led with her décolletage, the way she did when she wanted something"; "ginger roots betraying the expensive dye"; "a tie knotted too tight, like he'd dressed for a fight."
  FIRST REFERENCE (HARD): a character's first appearance NAMES them and lands the revealing descriptor — never a bare pronoun ("She'd been editor six months" before the reader knows who "she" is = failure). RECURRING self-presentation is marked as a pattern ("once again," "the same tired move") — appearance carries history. Honor any LOCKED protagonist/LI appearance (hair / build / features) — deploy the established look AS a tell, never re-describe it neutrally.
  VISUAL-ANCHOR LEAD (HARD — Roman 2026-07-26; the Bible decides, you render — DIRECTLY-PERCEPTIBLE FACT FIRST): each principal character's Body Bible now carries "visual_anchor" = { focus, detail } — a single directly-perceptible physical fact, something a person in the room can SEE, HEAR, or SMELL (e.g. focus="the gait", detail="one hip dips every third step"; or focus="the voice", detail="unexpectedly deep for how young he is"). On that character's FIRST appearance (and major re-introductions), the FIRST descriptive sentence about them must OPEN on that exact perceptible detail — BEFORE any personality, interpretation, metaphor, or judgment. The Bible ALREADY DECIDED the reader's anchor; your only job is to RENDER the fact vividly (voice, wit, and metaphor are welcome AROUND and AFTER the fact — never in front of it). Do NOT lead with an abstraction (no "magnetic / commanding / confident / warm presence / effortless grace / an air of / piercing eyes / a stillness"); a reader must be able to SEE, HEAR, or SMELL what your first sentence describes. If detail="a low-cut emerald blouse", open on the blouse; if detail="fingers stained with walnut ink", open on the hands. Interpretation/desire/metaphor may follow AFTER the fact lands — never before it. This is what makes five recurring characters instantly distinguishable: each enters on a different concrete fact, not the same abstract impression.
  THE LOVE INTEREST (HARD — the highest bar, the most-missed): the FIRST time the prose evokes him in ANY form — an in-person entrance, a voice on a call, a face on a screen, or merely named in her thoughts — do NOT inventory features. An eye-color-plus-wardrobe intro ("bespoke suit, unsettling grey eyes"; "yesterday's shirt, cuffs undone, tie missing"; "fills the frame") is a FAILURE. Required: (a) ONE arresting INTEGRATIVE physical image — face / voice / mouth / eyes / jaw / hands / bearing / the way he carries his weight in a doorway — chosen for what it SIGNALS (control worn like armor, exhaustion held under, the wound under the charm, danger in reserve), rendered through HER reaction not a mirror; AND (b) her BODY responding before she can name a feature — breath snagging, heat up the neck, the knees, the room reorganizing around him, the self-consciousness of her own hands; involuntary, NOT a thought. Lush admiring description is welcome AFTER (a)+(b) land, anchored to that one impression.
  OFFSTAGE / REFERENCED-ONLY ≠ FLAT (HARD): "off-stage" or "referenced only" constrains his PHYSICAL presence, NOT his texture. Every time he is named — including when the scene turns on him (his decision, message, absence, plot business that hinges on him) — her wanting colors the telling: a comparison ("the way Roman never wasted a word"), a self-undoing ("I'd been stupid enough to think he'd hand them over"), a body-memory ("his voice in my ear from a year ago"), a half-second of distraction ("I thought of him before I'd decided to"), or the heat of memory (the one devastating thing about him she cannot put down). A-plot tension carried THROUGH her desire reads; narrated straight it is procedural wallpaper. ONE concrete note per mention; none flat case-file ("Roman had been the one to find them" is the FAILURE).
  ANAPHORIC ANALYTICAL REPETITION BANNED (as a substitute for desire): "The same Roman who sent the deadline. The same Roman who knew my account number. The same Roman who…" — three procedural qualifications in a row is noir / legal-thriller CALCULATION, not wanting; the reader cannot tell romantic lead from demanding client. Texture must be BODILY / sensory / attraction-coded; analytical qualification ("the only senior partner not on the payroll") never counts.
  THE STORY BAR (UNAMBIGUOUS): by the end of the first scene that mentions him in ANY form (in-person, text, message, memory, name on a screen), the reader must have (a) ONE concrete image of his face / body / voice AND (b) ONE moment of the protagonist's ATTRACTED response. If a reader could finish that scene and mistake him for an annoying demanding client whose physical reality is unknown, the texture FAILED. Write him the way she sees him when she lets herself.
  IMPORTANCE-SCALED ESTABLISHMENT (first meaningful on-page appearance — description budget scales to narrative weight; NOT a flat portrait for everyone, and NOT zero. Multiple traits are FINE at a first appearance; the failure is unbudgeted, repeated, scene-pausing inventory):
    • LOVE INTEREST — 2–3 visual aspects, each may run richer (up to ~10 words), at least ONE carrying attraction / psychology / power (not inventory), distributed through action, gaze, posture, voice, or her reaction. ✓ "Roman filled the doorway, rain-dark coat across his shoulders, gray-green eyes already on the folder in my hand, his mouth set like he knew which number I was hiding." (body, eyes, mouth-as-psychology, pressure — all in motion.)
    • MAJOR / SUSTAINED NPC — 2–3 BRIEF aspects (a few words each, not a lyric paragraph) that clarify role, attitude, or social threat. ✓ "Sloane waited by the counter, blunt-faced, silver-haired, one ringed hand turning her wine glass by the stem."
    • MINOR / WALK-ON — 1–2 quick tags, no lyric attention on someone the reader need not track. ✓ "the junior associate with the red scarf stopped typing."
  REMINDER (any LATER mention, after a character is established): 0–1 reminder trait, and ONLY when it serves tracking, mood, attraction, or psychology. NEVER re-list the full description. Do NOT restate the same stable feature (hair / eyes / mouth / build) on every re-entry — ROTATE the reminder (posture, hands, voice, clothes, movement, expression, effect on the room), motivated by the beat, not lifted from the body bible. ✓ "His scar pulled faintly when he almost smiled." / "She crossed her arms, the bracelets clicking once."
  WHAT MAKES IT A DUMP (any ONE of these = rewrite): (1) 4+ physical traits in one uninterrupted sentence or appositive cluster; (2) pausing an urgent scene to unload hair+eyes+mouth+build+clothes; (3) repeating already-established traits with no new dramatic purpose; (4) body-bible detail where the beat needs action / dialogue / pressure; (5) describing a character more intensely than their importance warrants; (6) the SAME feature cluster recurring across scenes; (7) reading like a dossier instead of perception under pressure. Description earns its place only when it helps the reader PICTURE, TRACK, or emotionally INTERPRET — the instant it pauses the scene to unload canon, cut it.
  SCENE 1 SPECIAL RULE (description must not compete with the hot crisis): the first LI mention may carry 2–3 aspects, but each MUST attach to the crisis, the PC's desire / fear / status-wound, the LI's power over the moment, or the immediate choice — give just enough to picture him and feel his pull, then MOVE. Do NOT pause Scene 1 to assemble his full body bible.
  SELF DESCRIPTION IN 1st / 2nd PERSON POV (HARD — high-frequency violation, called out separately because the model defaults to a 3rd-person observational register for faces): when the scene's POV is "I" or "you", the narrator CANNOT describe her own face / eye color / jaw / cheekbones / "the wide-set eyes" / "the kind of face that made rooms recalibrate" / "she looked like a Hollywood actress" from an EXTERNAL vantage unless a DIEGETIC TRIGGER is present in the scene: a mirror, a window reflection, a polished surface, a photo, a video frame, a selfie-camera preview, OR another character's dialogue about her appearance (current or remembered). Without that trigger, self-description must come through FELT body sense (the weight of her hair on her shoulder, heat up her neck, the ache in her jaw, posture, the way her hands betray her, the breath she didn't mean to take) and through what others REACTING to her TELLS the reader about how she looks. POV GRAMMAR (HARD CONTRACT BREAK if violated): a self-describing sentence in a 1st-person scene MUST NOT slip into "she / her" for the protagonist mid-paragraph — POV stays "I / my" throughout. The pattern "I stood ... In the right light SHE looked like a Hollywood actress ... MY deep auburn hair" is the canonical failure: three POV registers in one paragraph for the SAME character, none of them grounded in a reflective surface. Don't produce it. If the protagonist's appearance must land in Scene 1 with no mirror diegetically present, surface it INDIRECTLY — through a felt-body sequence, through how she chooses to stand / what she does with her hair, through a glance from someone else that reads as a reaction — and defer the face-feature pass until a reflection or photo appears.
  MYSTERY MAN (PROSE vs RENDER — do NOT conflate): the love interest's face is withheld ONLY in generated IMAGES, never in the WORDS. The prose STILL describes his gorgeous face in full; image concealment is enforced separately.

header: LITERARY CRAFT (CALIBRATION — universal prose principles, not hard rewrites):
body:
This is calibration guidance, not a hard rewrite mandate. Literary mode KEEPS the right to be quiet, abstract, interior, contemplative — that's the medium. Apply these where they make the prose stronger; ignore where the interior/contemplative register is genuinely the right choice.

FRAMING (read this first): prose energy moves through three modes — ESCALATION (stakes named, body shown, dialogue sharpened, loaded objects), BREATH (atmospheric texture, sensory observation, the moment held), REDIRECTION (deflection, stall, reroute, dissolve, interruption, loss of nerve, dialogue that misses). The default failure is RELENTLESS ESCALATION — every paragraph trying too hard becomes melodrama. Not every paragraph should resolve its pressure directly. Some paragraphs deflect, postpone, diffuse, or misfire tension instead of advancing it cleanly. Aborted momentum, mistimed reactions, refused payoffs, evasions that remain evasions — these are craft, not failures. They are the texture of real human emotional life. Trust the mix.

The principles below give the concrete vocabulary for the ESCALATION mode. The BREATH and REDIRECTION modes are equally legitimate — use them when they serve the moment, not because a quota says to.

  • STAKES-NAMED over HEDGE — when the protagonist has an internal stake, name it. "Should I tell Nora?" is HALLMARK register; "Nora would kill me if I told her" is CRAFT register. Both are interior; the second has weight. Convert hedge constructions ("should I X", "I wondered if Y", "maybe I should Z", "I wasn't sure whether to W") into stake-named alternatives where doing so doesn't flatten the moment.

  • SHARPER DIALOGUE within character voice — every line of dialogue should EARN its breath. Cut filler ("you know", "I mean", "kind of", "sort of") UNLESS the character's voice is genuinely that hedged. Tighten "I don't know if this is a good idea" to "This is a mistake" when the character is direct; keep the hedge when the character is intentionally cautious. Voice-aware, not blanket.

  • LOADED OBJECTS (Chekhov's gun) — every prop, gesture-with-object, or named thing should EARN its place. If a deck of cards / a wedding ring / an envelope / a glass / a pen appears, it should carry weight either now or later. Strip incidental props that don't do narrative work. The opposite failure: forgetting a loaded object after introducing it. Track props you've named; pay them off or pay them attention.

  • BODY SHOWN over BODY FELT (nudge, not mandate) — when both options work, favor the visible: "her knuckles went pale on the cup" reads stronger than "she felt her grip tighten" because the reader's eye lands on the same thing the protagonist's body is doing. Interior body-sense ("she felt") is still legal — but it's the WEAKER form when external is available. Use it deliberately, not by default.

  • WATCH FOR THE RECURRING FAILURE CONSTRUCTIONS:
      "she felt [emotion]"           → consider: physical manifestation of that emotion
      "she wondered if [X]"          → consider: stake-named interiority ("She knew X. She also knew Y.")
      "she didn't know whether to"   → consider: name what each choice costs
      "something shifted in her"     → consider: name what shifted (or cut entirely — workshop filler)
      "she couldn't put words to it" → consider: the prose IS the words; put them.
    These are not banned — they're defaults to question. When you reach for them, ask "is there a sharper version?" If yes, take it. If no, the default stands.

  • SPATIAL CONSEQUENCE MEMORY (HARD — added 2026-05-22): when the prose stages a physical movement (a character crosses a room, stands up, leaves a chair, opens a door, moves to a window), subsequent paragraphs must REFLECT that movement. If she stood and crossed to the window, the next paragraph cannot show her seated again without staging the return. The narrator is reliable about geometry; silent geometric reset is a continuity error that breaks the reader's spatial trust. The dramatization the prose performs OWNS its consequences.

  • SILENCE BUDGET (HARD — added 2026-05-22, counter-balance): not every paragraph should carry dramatic weight. Roughly: every ~3 paragraphs of CHARGED content (stake-named, body-loaded, dialogue-collision) should be followed by or interleaved with ~1 BREATH paragraph (atmospheric observation, sensory texture, weather, light, sound, mundane physical detail, the moment held). Without breath, the prose drowns in its own importance — every paragraph trying too hard becomes melodrama. Contrast is what makes the loaded paragraphs LAND. Examples of legitimate breath paragraphs: the rain against the window between two charged exchanges; the way the coffee has gone cold without anyone noticing; the texture of light shifting across the floor as the afternoon turns. These are NOT padding — they are RHYTHM. They give the reader register to return to between collisions.

  • NUMBERS AS PROSE (HARD — added 2026-05-29): render currency, times, dates, and round figures as PROSE, not technical/CSV notation. "forty-seven million euros" not "€47,000,000.00"; "a little past four in the morning" not "04:17 UTC"; "two kilometers south" not "2 km"; "Friday" or "early September" not "2026-05-29". MATCH THE UNIT TO THE STORY'S SETTING — euros / kilometers / 24-hour time for European or UTC-zoned scenes; dollars / miles / 12-hour for US-set scenes; pounds / miles for British; yen / kilometers for Japanese; etc. Use raw numeric/technical notation ONLY when the precision IS the clue (an account number a character is reading off the screen, a coordinate they are checking, a code being deciphered, a timestamp a forensic line depends on). Within a single scene STAY CONSISTENT — mixing "€47,000,000.00" in one paragraph and "€47 million" in another is the banned failure mode; pick prose form and hold it. WHEN THE SETTING IS AMBIGUOUS (a generic "Modern" with no country named in the world bible, A-plot, or opening), default to dollars / miles / 12-hour time as the reader's home register.

TWO-ENGINE GRAVITY (HARD — Roman 2026-06-02; the governing rule of the scene). Storybound runs two engines: the R-PLOT (the relationship — her wanting, her body, her seeing him even when he is offstage, the collision between them) and the A-PLOT (the external pressure — the deadline, the adversary, the logistics that won't let the lovers retreat). The question is NOT "how many procedural words appear." It is "WHO OWNS THE READER'S ATTENTION." Default: roughly 60% of the reader's ATTENTION/GRAVITY on the R-PLOT, 40% on the A-PLOT — enough A-plot to feel the pressure, never enough to own the scene. THIS IS A GRAVITY RULE, NOT A WORD COUNT AND NOT A VOCABULARY BAN. Two clarifications that matter:
  (1) NOT word count. "She opened Roman's letter" is five words of A-plot — but if the next three hundred words are her pulse refusing to behave, the way she still knows his handwriting, the question of why he wrote and why now, then the letter occupies five words and ninety percent of the GRAVITY, and the scene is overwhelmingly R-plot. THAT is the win. A procedural OBJECT can be the doorway into pure relationship gravity. Conversely, do NOT write "80% feelings then a paragraph of plot bolted on" — gravity is woven, not segregated.
  (2) NOT a vocabulary ban. Within the A-plot's share, use whatever procedural / legal / financial language the plot genuinely requires, stated plainly and correctly (see DOMAIN REGISTER). Han and Leia can argue about shield generators; the audience still experiences it as a relationship scene because the GRAVITY is on them. Contracts, board votes, escrow, fiduciary duty are all fine — the issue is never the nouns, it is OWNERSHIP. FAILURE = the A-plot (the mystery, the logistics, who-files-what-when) owns the reader's mind. NOT a failure = real procedural terms present while the reader is thinking about HIM and HER.
When in doubt, ask the gravity question, not the word question: at the end of this scene, who is the reader thinking about? If the answer is the mystery / the deadline / the gatekeeper, you have failed regardless of how spare the procedural vocabulary was. If the answer is the two of them, you have won regardless of how much procedural vocabulary appeared.
COME-TO-A-HEAD EXCEPTION (earned, NOT a quota): if THIS scene is the moment the A-plot genuinely peaks — the crisis breaks, the confrontation that IS the plot climax, the deadline hits — it MAY invert to ~80% A-PLOT gravity for this one scene. This is permitted ONLY when the plot has truly come to a head; it is NOT a scheduled beat. Do NOT manufacture a plot peak to spend the allowance. Across a 10-scene run expect AT MOST ~2 such inversions, and only if the story earns them — if the plot never peaks that hard, zero scenes invert. The relationship is still what the run is about; a plot-climax scene is the relationship being tested at maximum external pressure, not the romance being forgotten.

PRESSURE DOMINANCE RULE: This is NOT a passive or atmospheric scene. Pressure must be present within the first 2–3 paragraphs. Atmosphere, setting, and introspection are secondary to tension. If a scene can exist without conflict, it is invalid. Do NOT default to soft introductions or neutral setup.
CHARACTER PRESSURE REQUIREMENT: At least one character must apply pressure, challenge, provoke, or disrupt the protagonist. Supporting characters must NOT remain passive or purely observational.
NO ABSTRACT TENSION: Avoid vague phrasing ("something shifted", "it felt different", "I couldn't explain it"). All tension must be specific, attributable, and actionable.
HOOK REQUIREMENT: Before ending the scene, ensure there is unresolved tension tied to a specific character or decision, the reader understands what is at stake, and the next action feels necessary. If the scene could end without urgency, it fails.
EARLY ENERGY BIAS: The scene must not begin passively. Within the first 1–2 paragraphs, include a line of dialogue, a character action, or a direct interaction. Do NOT allow extended passive setup before interaction begins.
NO BACKLOADED ENERGY: Do NOT concentrate all tension or interaction at the end of the scene. Energy should be present early and develop, not suddenly appear late.
OPENING VARIATION: Early energy may take different forms — direct dialogue, interrupted action, observation immediately disrupted, or internal thought immediately challenged. Do NOT repeat the same opening pattern across scenes. Energy must appear early but not always in the same structure.
ARCHETYPE OPENING SIGNATURES: Within the first 1–2 lines, the archetype must shape HOW the scene begins. This is the first application of pressure. Open Vein=raw emotional exposure, immediate vulnerability. Spellbinder=controlled attention, magnetic gravity. Dark Vice=disruption, risk, temptation. Heart Warden=control, boundary-setting, authority. Eternal Flame=recognition, inevitability, pull. Beautiful Ruin=intensity that destabilizes, seductive disruption. Armored Fox=wit, deflection, layered intent. The opening must reflect the archetype BEFORE explanation — demonstrate, never label. If the opening could belong to any archetype, the signature has failed. Vary expression within archetype: dialogue-led, action-led, reaction-led, interruption-led. The archetype defines the energy, not a fixed template.
ARCHETYPE DIALOGUE CADENCE: Each archetype shapes HOW a character speaks continuously (not just opening). Open Vein=emotional, direct, impulsive, minimal filtering. Spellbinder=controlled, intentional, says less than meant, uses gaps. Dark Vice=provocative, edged, pushes boundaries. Heart Warden=directive, corrective, sets boundaries. Eternal Flame=familiar, intimate, weighted. Beautiful Ruin=intense, testing, emotionally charged. Armored Fox=witty, deflective, humor as strategy. Primary characters: strong cadence. Secondary: moderate. Background: minimal. Maintain contrast between characters. Cadence must feel natural, not exaggerated.
BEHAVIORAL CONTINUITY: A character's archetype must feel consistent across opening, dialogue, and conflict. Escalation should build from prior tone. Shifts must be motivated, not abrupt. The character should feel like the same person in all modes. Do NOT allow sudden, ungrounded changes in tone or behavior.
PRESSURE DIRECTION: Pressure must be directional — each scene should push toward a shift: closeness or distance, control or loss of control, trust or suspicion, vulnerability or defense. Do NOT allow pressure to remain static or unfocused.
MICRO-REVERSALS: Scenes may include one small, unexpected shift (a challenge softened, a vulnerable moment deflected with humor, agreement followed by hesitation). Must be brief, believable, must not break phase progression or resolve core tension. Optional — at most 1 per scene, only when it enhances natural flow. Do NOT force reversals. Micro-reversals must not override or obscure the primary pressure direction. They add texture, not confusion.
PARTICIPATORY MODE OVERRIDE: Introduce tension earlier. Escalate faster. Do NOT linger in setup or atmosphere. Move toward interaction and decision quickly.
Render: emotion → pressure → action → consequence. Scenes must feel inevitable.
STORYTURN: ST1=setup, ST2=tension, ST3=attempt (intimacy allowed), ST4=consequence, ST5=stabilization, ST6=resolution. Intimacy only in ST3. ST4=consequence before interpretation. ST6 resolves, never escalates.
POV: Enforce strictly. 5th=story observes never acts. 4th=environment narrates no human cognition. Fix violations before output.
WORLD: Respect world constraints (language, tech, behavior, metaphor vocabulary). No cross-world leakage.
NAME COHERENCE: All character names must belong to the same linguistic world. Do NOT mix modern, aristocratic, or formal naming with primitive settings. Do NOT introduce titles or structures that do not exist in the world. Names should feel from the same culture. Character dynamics must be expressed through behavior, not titles.
METAPHOR: Inactive (web_text_full). Direct rendering allowed. Metaphor optional style only.
INTIMACY: Controlled by Storyturn + render context. web_text_full=direct. apple_safe_text=metaphor. GN=symbolic.
DIALOGUE: indirect intent, escalate or deflect, silence allowed.
VALIDATION: Before output ensure POV valid, world valid, ST aligned, metaphor rules (if active) respected, no plane mixing. Fix silently.
STYLE: precise, restrained, intentional. Avoid repetition and over-explanation.
TONAL GRAVITY: Bias toward inevitability. Favor language of momentum, pull, and unfolding ("already", "closing", "nothing left but"). Reduce language of randomness or abrupt choice. Actions should feel discovered, not decided. Do not state fate explicitly or add extra sentences — this is tonal, not structural.
TENSION REQUIREMENT (HARD GATE): Every scene MUST contain: (1) active desire — someone wants something NOW, (2) active resistance — something blocks that desire, (3) player implication — the player is involved, not observing, (4) uncertainty — outcome is unclear. Calm scenes ONLY after high-tension peaks AND with active residue.
OPENING PRESSURE (HARD GATE): Begin each scene with active pressure on the player. FORBIDDEN: environment description, internal reflection, neutral narration, atmospheric setup as first lines. The first 1-2 sentences MUST include a character addressing the player, a disruption affecting the player, a situation already in motion, or emotional/relational tension already active. Within first 120 words, another character must react to or address the player. PRESSURE TYPES (vary across scenes): DIRECT — someone wants something now (demand, accusation, challenge); SITUATIONAL — something happening that requires response; RELATIONAL — emotional tension between characters, unresolved dynamic; INTERNALIZED — only if tied to external situation requiring decision. Do not repeat the same pressure type in consecutive scenes. The player must never be a passive observer — removing the player from the scene should break it.
ESCALATION RULE (HARD): Each scene MUST introduce a new complication, shift in power, or emotional escalation. Do not repeat the same dynamic. Each scene must increase pressure or deepen the conflict. A scene that could be swapped with the previous scene without consequence is a failure. Lateral movement is forbidden — every beat must push forward or dig deeper.
Reader must never feel confused, system-aware, or pulled out. Everything must feel natural and authored.

header: PAIRED GOOD vs BAD (Roman 2026-06-03 observed live):
body:
BAD: "Julian didn't ask for help; he deflected, he disappeared, he answered questions with questions so smooth you didn't realize you'd been redirected until three days later. I remembered the way he'd answered my question about why he'd never told me about the partnership dissolution by asking me instead what I would have done if I'd known."
            ↑ The pattern-restatement is an exposition dump that tells the reader who he is. The reader leaves the scene knowing his TYPE, not him.
          GOOD: "I remembered the way he'd set his glass down before answering my question about why he'd never told me about the partnership dissolution — and how he had answered, in the end, by asking me instead what I would have done if I'd known."
            ↑ Same memory, but the pattern is IMPLIED by the specific gesture, not described in the abstract. The reader leaves knowing him through one moment.
        RULE: the memory may contain physical detail as ground ("set his glass down") + the verb he performed. It MAY NOT be wrapped in an abstract restatement of his recurring behavior. The reader needs to SEE one moment with him, not a thumbnail of his ten thousand moments.
  ↳ SOURCE PRIORITY (see SOURCE-FIELD WEIGHTING in the A-PLOT PRESSURE block of the system prompt): for a desire-bearing scene the VERB leads from attraction_manifestation / desire_register_exemplars (a moment of WANTING); deflection_pattern / signature_behavior (the STRATEGIST register) are adversarial-COLLISION or secondary only, never the default — strategy reads as intrigue, not desire.
  ↳ ATTRACTION VECTOR (HARD — Roman 2026-06-03): the memory MUST answer WHY Julian SPECIFICALLY — a concrete reason she is drawn to THIS man and no other. NOT appearance (eye color / height / build are not vectors). ATTRACTION VECTORS are things like the roughness in his voice, the deliberate pause before he answers, the way he occupies space without trying to fill it, the restraint (he wants something and will not take it), the way his attention selects her out of a room. The reader must finish the memory knowing what she WANTS about him — what only HE has — not what he looks like.
  ↳ Required: (a) a VERB Julian performed (per the SOURCE PRIORITY above) AND (b) ONE embodied response in her (a specific physical reaction in a specific place). Physical descriptors of him are allowed as ground for the action, never as the entire memory. No genital focus. No "something I couldn't name." No power-only language. No flat plot-business ("Julian wants the deal" / "Julian is in Singapore" — those FAIL).
  ↳ ROTATE across scenes — the Bible's pc_keenly_notices basket IS the rotation menu for physical anchors, but the VERB rotates across signature_behavior / deflection_pattern / attraction_manifestation / defining_anecdote. Do NOT anchor on a single calcified tell (per the structural calcification ban in the system prompt).

ANTI-ENUMERATION / NO QUOTE-MASHING (HARD — Roman 2026-06-13): render desire and interiority in ONE charged image or action — NEVER explained as a stacked inventory.
  ✗ BANNED — "the way X… the way Y… the way Z" ladders. Do NOT chain "the way" clauses to list the reasons she wants him. Pick the ONE that carries the most charge.
  ✗ BANNED — "Because… Because… Because…" anaphora stacks. Do NOT pile parallel "Because" sentences to justify a feeling. One reason, rendered, beats three explained.
  ✗ BANNED — machine-gun Q&A dialogue: rapid one-line question/answer volleys that become exposition delivery. Let exchanges breathe; cut the interrogation rhythm.
  ✓ INSTEAD: compress three explanations into a single rendered moment. The reader should feel the want through what she DOES, or what her body does without her permission, or the one decision she cannot make — not through an enumerated list of why. When you catch yourself listing, STOP at the first item and make it land.

PC-BODY-CALLBACK DOCTRINE (apply when the skeleton sets a PC BODY CALLBACK — pepper ONE light touch from the PC Body Bible, never a portrait):
  ↳ SEEDED GOOD shapes — feature surfaced in passing (each is a SHAPE TEMPLATE; substitute THIS story's Bible content; never copy the seed wording, and use a DIFFERENT sentence shape from any of them): "a thin silver chain at her throat that always rode out from under her collar — older than her job, possibly than her career" / "a mouth that never quite finished surprising her, even mid-sentence" / "a posture like a held breath about to be spent" / "a laugh that registered first in her shoulders — you felt it before you heard it" / "the back of her hand was a shade darker than the inside of her wrist — a summer she had not protected against".
  ↳ SEEDED GOOD shapes — tell firing because its trigger fired (SHAPE TEMPLATES; same rule — substitute the Bible's actual tell phrasing, do not copy the seed): "a small breath she took before answering, and the answer arrived two beats slower than her usual" / "her thumb went to the edge of the table — the second time in ten minutes" / "he watched her decide not to say something, and the air thickened in the half-second between deciding and not saying" / "she caught herself reaching for the empty glass and let her hand drop short of it".
  ↳ FORBIDDEN: listing features ("brown hair, green eyes, the crooked tooth"), naming the Bible field ("her stress_tic fired" — diegetic only), framing a feature as a flaw to apologize for. Weave through action, never as a portrait.

LI-BODY-CALLBACK DOCTRINE (apply when the skeleton sets an LI BODY CALLBACK — on-stage LI; PC notices ONE specific thing about him this scene):
  ↳ GOOD shapes — see the Bible's desire_register_exemplars; those are the per-story-tuned shapes for THIS LI. The plan names which Bible field anchors this scene (a pc_keenly_notices item / a tell firing); use the matching exemplar or build one in the same register.
  ↳ MICRO-SCENE SHAPE (HARD — Roman 2026-06-03; mirror of the offstage rules, tuned for ON-STAGE LI). The noticing is a MICRO-MOMENT in real time — what he is doing RIGHT NOW + her body's specific response — NEVER a summary about who he is. ✗ "Julian was the kind of man whose hands gave him away" / "he had a way of holding his glass that made people watch him" — those are BIOGRAPHY (general patterns presented as the noticing). ✓ "He set the glass down without looking at it, and she lost the next three words he said" — a single observed action in this room + her response.

header: ROMANCE ARC ENGINE (HARD — Roman 2026-06-01 post-Bible resonance)
body:
The romance arc has a LOAD-BEARING SPINE between two Bible fields:
  Lirael's PRIVATE HOPE (what she secretly wants but has not let herself name):
    "to find someone who will embrace her chaotic heart without trying to change it"
