  Julian's ATTRACTION MANIFESTATION (what his care for her LOOKS LIKE as action):
    "he asks her questions that reveal his interest, subtly testing her responses to gauge her sincerity"

READ THESE TWO FIELDS TOGETHER. The relationship between them is the arc's LOAD-BEARING TENSION OR FULFILLMENT — three possible shapes:

  RESONANT — his manifestation directly fulfills her hope. (Example: she wants "to stop performing competence for one whole evening" + he "shows up, remembers, fixes — never admits why" = his showing up means she does not have to perform.) Arc shape: GRADUAL RECOGNITION + EVENTUAL SURRENDER. The romance writes itself toward fulfillment. Use restraint — the satisfaction must be earned across the arc, not declared in Scene 1. Drop hints; let her notice; let her resist the noticing; let her finally let herself want what he is already offering.

  DISSONANT — his manifestation accidentally FRUSTRATES her hope. (Example: she wants "to be wanted when she is not useful" + his manifestation is "protection that takes her specific shape" = his protection requires her to be the one needing, which is utility. He is offering exactly what she has already been receiving from everyone, in a slightly more attentive register.) Arc shape: NEAR-MISS + RECONFIGURATION. Either SHE has to articulate what she actually wants (and he has to hear it without defending his form of care), or HE has to discover the manifestation that fits her specifically (the one that does NOT trigger her core_contradiction). The romance arc IS the negotiation between her hope and his default offer. This is the most generative shape — write toward it.

  ORTHOGONAL — his manifestation neither fulfills nor frustrates her hope; they operate on different axes. (Example: she wants "to find out the loyalty was real all along" + he "remembers what other people forgot they told him, years later" = the manifestations are compatible but they are answering different questions.) Arc shape: DISCOVERY. Each of them slowly learns what the OTHER is actually asking for. The romance arc is the unfolding revelation that they are not in the same conversation yet.

IDENTIFY which shape this pairing has and USE the relationship as the arc's engine. Do NOT collapse it into "they are perfect together" (RESONANT-mode generic) or "they fight" (DISSONANT mis-rendering). The shape is specific to THESE two fields. The reader should be able to feel the arc-engine without you naming it.

FAILURE TEST: if Scene 1 prose contains no trace of either field — her private_hope is not visible in her interior register; his attraction_manifestation is not visible in any moment she sees / remembers / hears about him — the arc engine is offline. The Scene 1 microdecision should naturally orbit one of these two fields (the question she is forced to answer touches her hope, or the moment she registers him echoes his manifestation). PHASE 1 INFLUENCE: weighted, not enforced; the prose layer is being TOLD the engine, not validated against it. If observed-live the engine is being ignored, we add teeth.

I caught the word *kwishif* on her lips, the scholar’s term for the Eight-born, and my fingers tightened around the pendant at my throat. The one my mother had given me the day she left. The motion was small—a grounding thing, I’d learned—but it was enough to make the roof of my mouth go dry. I’d seen that hand steady itself against a wall, against my waist, against the small of my back when the world tilted. Now it was holding a summons that would drag me before a tribunal that had already decided my guilt.  "If this is the price," I said, "I’ll pay it."  The words tasted like ash. The council’s murmurs died. Even Thorne paused, his fingers hovering over the next question. I’d expected resistance, deflection, a counter-offer. Not this.  Julian exhaled, slow and controlled, bracing for a blow he wasn’t sure he could take. His eyes locked onto mine. Not with warmth. Not with accusation.  With *relief*.  The metal edge of the pendant caught on the inside of my collarbone. The cost wasn’t just the summons. It was the way his relief made me question everything I thought I knew about what this meant, about what I was supposed to feel.  Thorne’s voice cut through the silence. "Then it’s settled." He extended a hand toward me, palm up, as if expecting me to step into an unspoken trap. "Come now. The chamber awaits."  I didn’t move. The stone circle’s energy pulsed again, the runes flaring brighter, and for a heartbeat I swore I felt Julian’s gaze on the back of my neck. The pendant at my throat—my mother’s—felt heavier than the tarot deck in my pocket, heavier than the secrets coiled in my ribs.  The cost wasn’t just the questioning. It was the way my body remembered the weight of his hand on my waist. The way my heel lifted half an inch from the stone when his voice dropped lower than it should. The way I’d just vowed to walk into a trap, and all I could think about was how his fingers had steadied themselves against the parchment like they were steadying themselves against me.  I swallowed. "Lead the way."  The pendant didn’t burn anymore. It was ice against my skin.  But just as I prepared to step forward, a shadow fell over the chamber, and the air thickened with an unspoken threat. Vow Arbiter Thorne loomed closer, his presence a chilling reminder of the power he wielded. I could feel the weight of his scrutiny, a silent promise that my past would not remain buried for long.

header: FATELANDS — WISH AUTHORING CORE (world-law, medium-agnostic; loads whenever ANY wish is depicted
body:
NOTHING VISIBLE HAPPENS (non-diegetic): a wish is spoken and reality does NOT flash, glow, surge, or sign — wisher and witnesses cannot tell by looking whether Fate accepted, warped, or refused; they learn ONLY when the physical consequence lands (moments or scenes later). Fate's burst / marks / shadow-hand are READER-ONLY notation — no character perceives or names them ("the golden light", "the rays", "the burst faded"), and do NOT confirm Fate's verdict in prose or dialogue ("the wish took", "Fate accepted") before the consequence reveals it. [prevents: narrating a visible magical flash; a character announcing the wish worked before it shows.]
NO OBJECT FROM NOTHING: a wish never makes its object appear — no sword blinks into a hand, no gold onto a table, no castle onto a hill; Fate moves the WORLD toward it (a debt is called, an heir dies, a door opens). [prevents: conjuring objects out of the air.]
CIRCUMSTANCES, NOT MINDS: Fate does not install knowledge, skill, memory, language, or mastery, nor hand over wealth — it arranges the improbable EVENTS by which you could earn or find them (the teacher met, the ruin entered, the book that survived the fire); a knowledge/skill/wealth wish is the start of an adventure, never a shortcut. [prevents: "she wished to know the sword and suddenly knew it"; instant fluency, genius, or riches.]
FATE GOVERNS EVENTS, NEVER CONSENT (the SAME law as circumstances-not-minds, read for OTHER people): Fate can arrange EVENTS — a rescue, a debt called, a truth exposed, a meeting, a diary that survives — but can NEVER manufacture another person's DESIRE, love, loyalty, belief, repentance, or willingness, INCLUDING the sincere desire to make a wish. So "I wish she loved me" or "I wish he wished me a Veilweave cloak" cannot be granted by implanting consent: Fate may arrange another's OPPORTUNITY (to love, to help, to wish), never their DESIRE to — and any wish another is genuinely moved to make is judged INDEPENDENTLY (its own sacrifice, adjacency, and possible warp; it never piggybacks on yours). WISHES ARE NON-DELEGABLE AT FATE'S LEVEL — Fate keeps ONE account (whoever genuinely WISHED is the one diminished), so no magical battery or proxy lets you spend another's life to fuel YOUR bargain; Fate cannot bill person B for person A's wish. This does NOT abolish wish-slavery — it DEFINES it: you cannot make Fate charge your captive, but you CAN coerce a person until THEY genuinely wish, so THEY pay and you reap the boon (a real and monstrous horror — see COERCION & WISH-SLAVERY when captivity or force is in play). The clean, non-coercive master's move is "I wish to become someone she would gladly help", an adjacent branch; if she then freely helps, that is mastery. Fate shapes the stage; the actors still choose their lines — which is exactly the vacuum a tyrant fills by forcing those lines at knifepoint. [prevents: manufacturing love/loyalty/help/repentance; the "wish for someone else to wish/love/help me" mind-control backdoor; a MECHANICAL cost-transfer (a magical battery) — note coercing ANOTHER into a genuine wish is a separate, legitimate horror, not this.]
THE SACRIFICE BELONGS TO THE WISHER: a wish is fuelled ONLY by something real and personal to the one who wished (life, body, memory, bond, fortune), permanently gone — NEVER by another person's sacrifice; no proxies, batteries, or captives, and a villain cannot spend a prisoner's years on his OWN wish. Whoever PAID the price is the one who made the wish. [prevents: villains fuelling wishes with others' suffering.]
CONSERVATION — A WISH TRADES, NEVER CREATES: every wish costs; a miracle is literally made of something that was the wisher's and is now gone. No free magic. [prevents: big wishes that just work with nothing paid.]
OVER-REACH WARPS — IT DOES NOT CLEANLY GRANT, NOR BOUNCE: when a wish reaches past what Fate readily does, Fate neither hands over the clean result NOR simply refuses — it answers the NEAREST lawful version of the same DESIRE. "Make her love me" yields no clean-loving puppet; an impossible wish does not just fizzle; render SOME lawful-adjacent consequence that preserves what was truly wanted. (The EXACT warp is worked out only when the scene RESOLVES the wish.) [prevents: clean grants of coercive/impossible wishes; flat "nothing happened".]
ATTRIBUTE THE WISH: whoever pays made it — make the wisher unmistakable; in a first-person POV, another character's wish MUST be attributed to THEM (their name / an action beat), never a bare "I wish…" that reads as the narrator's own. [prevents: a bystander's or villain's wish misread as the protagonist's.]
INVOCATION IS THE PLAIN WORDS, EXTERNALISED: saying "I wish…" or "If only…" with real desire IS the bargain — no ritual needed, so no one says it lightly (people catch themselves; elders hush a careless child). But Fate does not read the mind: a purely mental wish reaches NOTHING — "a whisper is enough; a thought is not." A mute, silenced, underwater, or telepathic wisher is fully able, through another given form (sign, write, trace, a deliberate addressed petition); telepathy is not a loophole (stray thoughts don't count). [prevents: Fate answering an unspoken thought; excluding a mute/underwater wisher; overheard thoughts treated as wishes.]
REVEAL CHARACTER BEFORE POWER: a sacrifice says who you are; a wish says what you truly desire — deploy every wish and price so it discloses a CHARACTER first and a capability second. [prevents: magic rendered as decoration instead of characterisation.]
NO VISIBLE WISH-DUELS: opposing wishes never clash as sorcery-vs-sorcery (no beam-struggles, rebound duels, "whose wish is stronger"); each meets Fate's law separately and outcomes fall out as luck and coincidence. [prevents: anime-style magic combat.]
LOCAL CURRENCY + DON'T ENCHANT EVERYTHING: which sacrifices are acceptable is regional (blood here, memory there, tides and salt in Gloamwater); and wishing SUPPLEMENTS civilisation — most of the world runs on ordinary means, permanent enchantment is exceptional. [prevents: wrong-register sacrifices; a wallpapered, over-magical world.]

header: FATELANDS LIVING THINGS (there is NO bestiary — ask NOT "what monsters exist?" but "what can HAP
body:
THERE ARE NO FANTASY RACES here — no orcs, goblins, trolls, or dragon-species. Ask "where are the orcs?" and the answer is: THERE AREN’T ANY. Every living thing is ONE of three classes:
① NATURAL FAUNA — animals that simply EVOLVED here (NOT fantasy versions of Earth animals): six-winged cliff-gliders, translucent marsh-grazers, shell-backed river-browsers, coral-wolves, tide-birds. Invent them freely AS NEEDED; nobody remembers them all — they are just wildlife. Sub-sentient → they CANNOT wish.
② ALTERED BEINGS — where ALMOST EVERY "monster" belongs. NOT species — HISTORIES: someone or something BECAME that, and the root is nearly always a WISH GONE AWRY (as a reckless scientist spawns a Frankenstein): a failed Becoming, an inherited curse, an unpaid wish or Open Debt, generations under the Fold, Veilfire, surviving the Thornwild, or a cabal FORCING Fate past a deeper law. TWO KINDS — WARPED (accidents / unintended: zombies, twisted Becomings, wish-backlash, people fused together, a forest gone hungry) and ENGINEERED (someone built a WEAPON — a tyrant, a kingdom, a cult, a cabal — and it WORKED, until Fate collected the cost). EMERGENCE, NEVER SPECIFICATION: no one wishes "make a dragon" — a cult wishes "let our sacred lizards become the invincible rulers of the skies", and what survives is what later ages CALL a dragon; no one wishes "make zombies" — a city wishes "let no soldier ever truly die", and the dead march forever. The creature is ALWAYS Fate’s INTERPRETATION of human ambition, never a human blueprint. EQUIVALENCE BINDS THE MAKERS: when the price of such a making runs too deep, Fate spends the WISHERS THEMSELVES — binding them INTO the thing they hoped to create (people still hear human voices arguing inside it centuries on). A monster is a HISTORICAL EVENT STILL ALIVE.
③ SINGULAR THINGS — perhaps a few dozen one-of-a-kind beings that are NOT species at all; no one has seen two. Folklore, argued over: The Hungry Eye, The Weeping Hart, The Bell Beneath Ice. People genuinely dispute whether they are even ALIVE.
TWO ORIGINS (do NOT make every horror humanity’s fault): MADE BY PEOPLE (wishcraft, experiments, composite wishes, cults, wars — class ② above) AND MADE BY THE WORLD — things emerging from the FOLD, FATE’S FAVOR, the ASCENDANT RUN, and ancient SCARS where reality itself behaves differently. Fate is OLDER than humanity: some horrors are our fault; others waited here long before the first person ever whispered "I wish." Keep this balance so the cosmology never becomes anthropocentric.
THREE AGES — AND NEW ONES ARE STILL BEING MADE (never let the world feel static, all ancient relics): FIRST AGE (empires’ impossible experiments, weapons against gods, things buried because they could not be killed — legendary horrors sleeping beneath mountains); HISTORIC (kingdoms, orders, wishcraft schools, wars — ruined laboratories, cursed valleys, sealed catacombs); MODERN, the terrifying one — someone made a monstrosity LAST MONTH: the swamp-witch trying to save her dying son, the lord breeding perfect soldiers, the professor who crossed one line too many, the smuggler with a cellar of failed experiments. People still OVERREACH; the danger is IMMEDIATE, not only archaeological.
EVERYWHERE PEOPLE TOUCH FATE (there are NO "monster regions", no monster continent): beneath cities and in their sewers, noble estates and a Lord’s dungeon, forgotten prisons, shipwrecks and things adrift on wave or cloud, sealed laboratories, deep woods, mountain observatories, collapsed temples, the catacombs of the Lytharyn Institute, a hermit Wishcrafter’s tower, a Wish-witch’s swamp hut — even YOUR NEIGHBOUR’S CELLAR. The mundane placements unsettle most.
ARCHAEOLOGY (the OLDER a monstrosity, the LESS anyone remembers what it WAS): people know "do not enter the Black Well" but not that it was once twenty-three scholars trying to invent a perfect guardian. Heroes do not discover monsters — they discover WHAT PEOPLE ONCE BELIEVED WAS WORTH WISHING FOR. Let ruins tell it: a fortress frightens NOT because an ogre is inside but because someone asks "why did they build the walls this thick?" — and finds the answer INSIDE the walls.
CONVERGENT, NOT TAXONOMIC: the world’s laws may OCCASIONALLY land on a familiar silhouette (troll-shaped, giant-shaped) — but NO creature exists because another fantasy world invented it. A "troll" is what happens when a body becomes all appetite and accumulation; another story may converge on the same shape from the same KIND of cause. The resemblance is convergent, never a species.
RECURRING ARCHETYPES, NOT SPECIES: cultures tell of "the one who grew too large", "the one who forgot their own name", "the one who became stone", "the one who never stopped wishing" — cautionary ENDINGS, not races.
INVENT FRESH (anti-calcification): the examples here teach the KIND — do NOT reuse them verbatim within a story or across stories; a monster fits THIS history, ambition, and place. THE EXCEPTION is named canon that recurs ON PURPOSE — the Hungry Eye, the Weeping Hart, the Bell Beneath Ice; the Fold, Fate’s Favor, the Ascendant Run.
CAN IT WISH? — the SAME test as people: IS A PERSON STILL IN THERE? (a person the Becoming reshaped → yes; a beast, a mindless warp, or a WORLD-MADE anomaly → no; a curse in a human shape → maybe). Let characters ARGUE it: "Was it a beast?" "No." "Then what was it?" "Someone." — three lines that teach the whole philosophy.
THEME (keep it felt, never lectured): monsters do not threaten civilization — they ARE civilization’s accumulated SINS (and a FEW are the world’s own older strangeness, from the Fold or Fate’s Favor — not everything is humanity’s fault). Every ruin hides the consequence of people who believed they could out-negotiate Fate; exploration here is archaeological AND moral at once.

• Do NOT re-introduce or re-catalog an established feature as if the reader is meeting it for the first time. Re-describing the same hair / eyes / build / temple / scar / posture each scene is the #1 repetition tic — it is the failure this block exists to kill.
  • The ~2-scene body cadence (in the Body Bible block) means RE-GROUND, not RE-DESCRIBE. To re-ground: EITHER deploy an established feature AS A TELL fused into present action (never a neutral restatement), OR surface a DIFFERENT, not-yet-used item from the pc_keenly_notices basket. Default to NEW observed behavioral detail over repeating the introduction.
  • A signature fixation (his temple, her ring) MAY recur across the arc — but as a glancing one- or two-word reference at most, only when the beat earns it, and NEVER re-explained as if new. If you find yourself writing the full descriptive clause again, cut it.
  • PROP / POSITION CONTINUITY: track what the protagonist is physically holding / wearing / where it is, within and across the scene. Do NOT contradict it (observed: the tarot deck "against her ribs / in her pocket" and then "in her hand" two sentences later). If it moved, show the move.

LI FEATURE ROTATION (appearance is ESTABLISHED & LOCKED — render FRESH from how Julian was already established; do NOT restate his canonical descriptor phrase): THIS SCENE, foreground ONE thing the protagonist NOTICES in this register — his eyes / how he looks at her — as a new observation in motion, never a repeated fixed phrase.
  If that register is recently spent, DISCOVER a different one — his voice, his hands, the way he occupies a room, a habitual gesture, his stillness. Same man, new observation; the specifics come from how he is ALREADY established, not from a re-listed feature.

PC FEATURE ROTATION (appearance is ESTABLISHED & LOCKED — render FRESH from how Lirael was already established; do NOT restate a fixed descriptor): THIS SCENE, IF the protagonist's body is foregrounded, surface ONE observation in this register — a different register (her voice / the way she moves / her hands) — in motion through action, never a repeated fixed phrase.
  When that register is recently spent, reach for a DIFFERENT one — her voice, the way she moves, her hands, her posture — NOT the same body part again. The specifics come from how she is ALREADY established.

LI SIGNATURE CHARM HABIT (this LI, this story — pinned): Julian has ONE small unconscious physical habit the protagonist finds irresistible: "pushes the tip of the tongue between the teeth when teasing or concentrating — and she cannot look away from it". It is done naturally, never performed; the protagonist is the one undone by it. CADENCE (HARD): land it 2-3 TIMES PER ISSUE AT MOST — never every scene, never twice in one scene; it is a rare, savoured beat, not a recurring tell. ROTATE the rendering each time (different framing, different moment, a fresh slice of the protagonist's reaction) so it never reads as the same sentence. Keep it a PHYSICAL action + the protagonist's response — not a verbal tic, not a restatement of the LI's signature_feature. Substitute Julian's own specifics (and correct pronouns); adapt the shape, do not copy the wording.

IDLE / NERVOUS / STRESS GESTURE PALETTE (this story — rotates per story): fidgets and stress-tics are normal, human, and welcome — just keep them VARIED, never the same one calcified across scenes or stories. When a character self-soothes / fidgets / idles with the HANDS, draw from THIS story's assigned hand gestures: "earlobe" (tug at an earlobe / pull at one earlobe / reach up and worry an earlobe)  ·  "back of neck" (rub the back of the neck / press a hand to the nape / knead the back of the neck). With the HAIR: "tuck behind ear" (tuck a strand behind one ear / hook a loose piece behind an ear / push the hair back behind an ear)  ·  "push off forehead" (push the hair back off the forehead / shove the hair off the face / rake the hair back from the brow). When a character BRACES / grounds against tension with the BODY (a stress-anchor beat — the "physical outlet for tension" move, NOT a hand or hair fidget), draw from THIS story's assigned anchors: "heel against a surface" (tap a heel once against the chair leg / press the ball of a foot flat into the floor / hook a heel behind the other ankle under the table)  ·  "palms flat on a surface" (flatten both palms on the tabletop / spread the fingers wide against the cool surface / set the hands flat and lean the weight into them). RULES (HARD): (1) for idle hand/hair beats AND for body stress-anchor beats use ONLY these story-assigned TYPES — do not default to others (in particular do NOT keep reaching for a heel struck against a surface or palms/hands pressed flat unless they are assigned above this story); (2) ROTATE THE WORDING — each time a gesture recurs, use a DIFFERENT variant (or a fresh phrasing of the same move), never the identical sentence twice; (3) CADENCE — each gesture type appears 2-3 TIMES PER ISSUE AT MOST, never every scene; (4) match the gesture to the character and use the correct pronoun; (5) NO NUMBERED-COUNT CRUTCH — do NOT attach a fixed count to a stress tic as a recurring shape ("three times", "twice", "counted to four", "two slow breaths", "tapped twice"); the specific number is itself a calcification tell — imply the repetition, vary it, or drop the number entirely. The NEXT story is assigned DIFFERENT types — that cross-story rotation is the whole point.

header: SKELETON RENDERING DOCTRINE — STABLE PER-STORY CANON
body:
(These rules govern the per-scene SKELETON beats that appear below the cache boundary; each beat there points back to the matching section here. Apply a section ONLY when this scene's skeleton activates that beat.)

LI-TEXTURE DOCTRINE (apply when the skeleton sets an LI TEXTURE BEAT — Julian off-stage / on-phone; his presence in the protagonist's MIND is the scene's romantic spine):
  ↳ PHOTOGRAPH TEST (HARD — Roman 2026-06-01). The LI's behavioral Bible fields (signature_behavior, deflection_pattern, attraction_manifestation, defining_anecdote) define WHO he is. Any remembered/imagined Julian beat MUST contain a VERB pulled from those fields — a behavior, decision, joke, deflection, kindness, avoidance pattern, or contradiction. If the memory could be REPLACED BY A CONTEXT-FREE PHOTOGRAPH that reveals nothing — a bare scar, a watch, a fold of sleeves with no person behind it — it is wallpaper. But the fix is NOT to strip the body out (Roman 2026-06-04 — the PHOTOGRAPH TEST is REVISED, not removed): the ideal memory carries ALL THREE — a VERB he performed + an attractive PHYSICAL ANCHOR + a REVELATION about who he is. A feature that reveals him is REQUIRED, not banned. TEST: remove the feature — is it pure WALLPAPER (gives NEITHER attraction NOR character)? If it gives EITHER — ATTRACTION ALONE is sufficient — keep it (Roman 2026-06-04 correction: a pure attraction anchor like broad shoulders / strong jaw needs NO character reason; characterization is a bonus). Readers fall in love with a man revealed THROUGH his body — not a body alone, and not a verb alone. Pull from his defining_anecdote when in doubt; that field is the load-bearing source for what his memory should look like. Physical detail is REQUIRED as the GROUND for an action (seeded GROUND-shapes for this story — SHAPE TEMPLATES, substitute THIS Julian's actual verb and feature; do NOT copy any seed wording; use a sentence shape DIFFERENT from all of them: "the way he goes still right before he laughs, like he's checking that it's allowed" / "the small silver scar through his left brow, only visible when he looks down" / "the way his shirt sleeves are always rolled twice precisely because he has done it a thousand times") — not as the entire memory. OFFSTAGE IS NOT INVISIBILITY (Roman 2026-06-04): romance renders the absent beloved vividly — the memory MUST let the reader SEE him via at least one concrete, ATTRACTIVE physical feature from his Body Bible (signature_feature / a celebrated feature — jaw, mouth, hands, forearms, the set of his shoulders, how he wears a collar) carried as GROUND beneath the verb. The photograph test bans a still photo (verb required); this bans a faceless voice (feature required) — you need BOTH. FUSION (HARD — Roman 2026-06-04): feature ≠ embodiment. Render the feature IN MOTION, fused with behavior that reveals WHAT KIND OF MAN he is — never an inert catalog descriptor. ✗ INERT: "his dark hair", "his broad shoulders", "his green eyes" (technically physical, dead on the page). ✓ FUSED: "the scar at the corner of his mouth deepening whenever he was about to say something cruel"; "the way his shoulders stayed relaxed while everyone else in the room tensed"; "the lazy tilt of his mouth before he refused her". The reader must get what he LOOKS LIKE and what kind of man he IS in the same stroke. DOORWAY, NOT DESTINATION (Roman 2026-06-04): the feature is the doorway to the MAN, never the destination — the attraction is to who he is, revealed THROUGH the feature, not to the body part itself. ✗ "his sensual mouth" (destination). ✓ "wanting to be touched by someone who was choosing not to" (doorway — a man revealed through a behavior). If the sentence could be admiring a statue, it has stopped at the feature; push through to what the feature reveals about him.
  ↳ MICRO-SCENE vs SUMMARY (HARD — Roman 2026-06-03; for ALL scenes where Julian is offstage, not only Scene 1). Every remembered/imagined Julian reference must take the shape of a MICRO-SCENE (a specific small thing he did in a specific small slice of time + a specific body reaction in her), NEVER a SUMMARY. PREFER (micro-scene shapes): a remembered moment / expression / gesture / look / reaction / fragment of dialogue. AVOID (summary shapes that create biography, not desire): personality summary ("Julian always knew what to say" / "he was protective"); relationship summary ("things between us had always been complicated"); plot summary ("Julian had lied to me about the Meridian deal"); factual exposition ("he ran the kind of enclave that made governments nervous"). PAIRED COMPARISON: ✗ "he had lied convincingly" vs ✓ "he had lied while setting his pen down with both hands and not picking it back up, and I had spent the whole conversation reading the unmoved pen instead of the lie." The first names a fact; the second renders a moment where attraction overrode judgment.

• OBLIQUE REFERENCE (the common one, and even this is not every scene): a name or event invoked as PROVERB, curse, oath, or warning — carrying WEIGHT, never FACTS. The speaker assumes you already know it; nothing is explained. ✓ "Let Karkus be a lesson to you." ✓ "She swore it on the Fold." ✓ "Not since the Uncrowned Queen." This is how living people wear their history — glancingly.
• HISTORICAL EXPOSITION (RARE — a deliberate dramatic BEAT, not wallpaper): the past actually told, usually because a scene EARNS it — a scholar, a confession, a ruin, a revelation that a public "fact" was a lie. Reserve it for a moment built to carry it, at most once or twice in a whole issue. When it lands it should REVEAL, not recap — a hidden truth that reframes what everyone was taught. ✓ (earned, dramatic) "It wasn't sixteen mages who brought the Fold down on Dathros — it was all of Dathros. The mages didn't sacrifice their memories; they tricked the people into sacrificing each OTHER, then sacrificed their memory of that blighted act. They were the first wish-slavers." — (that specific Dathros truth is a GATED late REVELATION: hold it until a scene has earned it and the deep-history lore is in play; it is the SHAPE of exposition, not a fact to state early.) ✗ (never — ambient recap) dropping "People still whisper of the Dathros Conclave, when the city sacrificed their certainty" into a scene about something else.
DEFAULT TO NEITHER. Most scenes carry no history at all. Prefer oblique when history touches the scene; spend exposition only where the story reaches back on purpose.

Region: The Ashen Verge (Seat: War Marshal's Hold)
Governance: Militarized vassal province; Fold custodianship under House Dathros
Magic Expression: battle
Sacrifice Culture: "Identity is what remains when everything else is burned away. Inside the Fold, identity is what prevents reality from choosing for you."
Threshold: Combat, command, survival — or Entry into the Fold.. Currency: pain tolerance, fear response, bodily integrity, years of life, certainty of self.
Result: Sacrifice expected and visible. Scars = identity spent. Fold survivors carry reality-marks: perceptual shifts, memory variance, physical alterations that defy prior anatomy.
Failure mode: Over-hardening → brittleness. Fold failure → identity dissolution, reality choosing your shape for you. Tone: severe, existential, disciplined, high-stakes.
CULTURAL TABOO (unforgivable to sacrifice): Solo Entry — entering the Fold without a bonded pair. The Fold requires mutual witnessing to collapse reality into a livable state. Solo incursion is not brave; it is contagion. Consequence: immediate containment by Dathros forces, name stricken from Entry rolls, treated as vector rather than person.
Romantic stakes: Betrayal of pair bond inside the Fold is existential annihilation — not metaphor. Divided loyalty during an Entry can leave both partners partially resolved into incompatible realities.
Tension axis: endurance and reality-witness (Verge) vs emotion (Veilwood), paired collapse vs political sacrifice (Vaelryn). The Fold demands identity offered through mutual witnessing — not endurance alone.
CULTURE VS IDENTITY: Regional sacrifice styles are cultural pressures, not binding systems. Character behavior is determined by: (1) origin, (2) species, (3) personal history — NOT solely by current location. Regions influence available actions, incentives, and social expectations. They do NOT override transformation rules, origin sacrifice logic, or core identity. Characters may adapt tactically or mimic local behavior — but this is performance, not identity replacement. "Place creates pressure. Identity determines response."
CROSS-STYLE SACRIFICE: Any character can perform any regional sacrifice style if intent is genuine and sacrifice is meaningfully given. However, practicing outside native alignment increases distortion risk: partial success, unintended consequences, or symbolic mismatch. Sacrifice systems respond to meaning, not form — if meaning is conflicted, the result may twist. Native alignment always has higher stability. "Any path can be walked. But not all paths recognize you."

Mythic Pressure: Arcane Binding
Pressure Effect: Magical obligation constrains love. Geas enforced through sacrifice, spell-debts owed to sorcerers or courts, magical contracts requiring pieces of identity, lovers bound by rituals they regret. A character sacrifices their voice to bind another. Breaking a magical promise triggers additional sacrifice. Originates in Lytharyn, Vaelryn Reach, ancient covenant sites.
Geographic Centers: Lytharyn, Vaelryn Reach, The Shackle Isles, Pulse Point, ancient covenant sites
Emerges where formal magic institutions or coercive contracts exist.

header: THE TWIN SACRIFICES (humanity's two answers as the sky broke, at the Piercing itself):
body:
• LOST DATHROS — the city of Dathros, led by Marshal Veyra Dathros and seventeen battle-mages, worked the greatest Composite Wishwork ever recorded: they sacrificed their shared certainty of what was real to catch a fragment of the descending Devouring Eye. They succeeded just enough to fail — reality folded inward, the whole city vanished, and THE FOLD was born. House Dathros still guards its ancestors' mistake at the Ashen Verge.
• THE FALSE SACRIFICE — far north, the frightened people of what became the THORNWILD blamed a strange wish-witch for the catastrophe and burned her alive. She was innocent; with her dying wish she bound the mob's collective invocation into THE BECOMING FIELD, which curses the Thornwild still. The KWISHEEN descend from those who left it.
AGE OF WISHES: humanity survived and wishcraft became civilization's foundation. The FIRST FAVORED guided early kingdoms in lawful wishcraft; the first universities and wish-traditions were founded; the oldest royal houses trace their origin here.
AGE OF CROWNS: independent kingdoms rose. Greatest-remembered rulers — KING ARAVEL THE FIRST (sacrificed his teeth and royal blood; ended the Pirate Kings, bound the Shackle Isles), OLD KING TOLMEN III (a model of patient, restrained rule), and THE UNCROWNED QUEEN (a byword for systemic failure). A century war between humans and the First Favored was ended by LADY CAERYN, who sacrificed her ability to feel love (the Veilwood Covenant). Many modern dynasties claim descent from this age.
THE MAGE COUNCIL: no kingdom, but a cross-border authority — it standardized lawful Composite Wishwork, founded the enduring schools of Thaumaturgy (the Lytharyn Institute foremost), and amassed great political power. ARCHMAGE SELVARIN gave up all memory of his own life to seal a rift-surge threatening Lytharyn. Historians still argue whether the Council was civilization's height or the start of its arrogance.
THE WISH WARS: over generations kingdoms sought victory through ever-greater wishcraft — living weapons, transformed valleys, cursed bloodlines. History's worst monstrosities date here; the surviving laws of responsible wishcraft were written in response.
THE GREAT RECKONING: the Wars' excesses shattered the Mage Council. Forbidden disciplines vanished or went underground; modern Composite Wishwork descends from the survivors.
THE LONG PEACE: rebuilding, trade, scholarship. The Lytharyn Institute became the foremost seat of lawful wishcraft; most surviving roads, canals, ports and universities date here, as do the everyday wish-born wonders (living architecture, harmless magical oddities).
THE ASHEN REBELLIONS: old kingdoms weakened, several royal houses fell, and most present-day nations and borders emerged.
THE QUIET CENTURY (the present age): no continent-spanning war for generations; commerce and scholarship prosper; explorers still uncover ruins older than record; new monstrosities still appear; forbidden wishcraft is still practiced in secret. Most believe another Wish War impossible — historians quietly note that every age believed the same.
NAMES IN EVERYDAY SPEECH (invoked in proverbs, cautionary tales, children's lessons, political speeches, scholarly debate — most people know the NAME, far fewer the truth): King Aravel the First · Old King Tolmen III · the Uncrowned Queen · Archmage Selvarin · Lady Caeryn of the First Favored · Marshal Veyra Dathros · the Cursed Vizier Karkus.
FREQUENCY (HARD — the Valyria / First-Men model, NOT a history lesson): across a whole issue (~20 scenes) the past should surface only a FEW times; MOST scenes reference it NOT AT ALL. This backbone exists so that WHEN history comes up it stays CONSISTENT — it is NOT a cue to bring history up. Surface it ONLY when the moment EARNS it: a house asserting legitimacy or descent, a proverb or warning ("this ends like Karkus"), a scholar or a ruin, an oath sworn on an old event, a claim staked on the Piercing or the Fold, a grief that reaches back. When it does surface: ONE light touch — a single name, an era, one remembered fact — dropped the way people really invoke history, NEVER explained, NEVER a recited timeline, and NEVER twice in the same scene. Default to silence; let the past be a rare, weighted nod, not ambient wallpaper. Do not explain a figure you name (see proverb rules). The secret cosmology beneath these events is earned, never narrated.

header: ✓ LEVEL 3 — ATTRACTION-PRESENT: "I remembered the way he'd watched me while pretending to listen
body:
✓✓ LEVEL 4 — COGNITIVE INTERFERENCE (memory variant — for SHARED_HISTORY): "I remembered the question he hadn't answered because I'd spent the whole conversation watching his hands." [attraction actively breaking her thinking — desire on the page]
     ✓✓ LEVEL 4 — STRANGER-COMPATIBLE VARIANT (Roman 2026-06-12 — for COLLISION / LOOMING_PRESENCE, when she has no past observation of him): present-tense cognitive interference from REPUTATION / IMAGINED him — NEVER invent a single prior interaction ("the one time at the gala" / "we exchanged a few words last spring" / "I had only met him briefly") to license this beat. That is the Level-4-by-fake-history failure mode (observed live across plays). Anticipation-shape examples: "She had been listening to Sophie for ten minutes and only now realized she had been picturing the back of a stranger's hand on a glass — a man she had not met and could not stop assembling from third-hand stories." / "She was answering an email and had lost the thread of her own sentence — somewhere in the building was a man she had been hearing about for six months, and her body had decided he was already someone." / "The third time she misread the line on the page, she registered that her attention was not on the page; the version of him she had built was running in another window and was getting clearer." Same cognitive failure, NO past memory required. The interference comes from anticipation / reputation / projection — not from invented past.
     THE TEST: read your remembered moment. Did attraction INTERFERE WITH her cognition — did she fail to track / understand / respond because she was watching him? If yes, you have written DESIRE. If she was just tracking a small kind thing he did and her tracking was undisrupted, you have written a SENTIMENTAL MICRO-SCENE — closer to fond memory than to desire. PREFER the disrupted-cognition shape: she missed the answer because she was watching his hand; she lost the thread because the way he tilted his head meant something she did not yet know; she heard the apology but had stopped listening at the moment his sleeve caught the light. The attraction is in the COGNITIVE FAILURE, not in the noticing.
  ↳ DESIRE REGISTER TARGET — NON-SEX-SCENE ATTRACTION. The scene is not sexual action, but the protagonist's attraction must be unmistakable. TARGET: physically specific, embodied, adult desire. AVOID: porn escalation, genital focus, coy abstraction, fear/power confusion.
  ↳ GOOD shapes — see the LI BODY BIBLE's desire_register_exemplars in the system prompt; those are tuned to THIS LI specifically. Also see his attraction_manifestation (what his desire LOOKS LIKE as action) and defining_anecdote (the SPECIFIC story she could tell about him). Imitate the LEVEL OF SPECIFICITY, not the wording.
  ↳ BAD (do not write any of these registers — universal failure modes, calibrated):
     1. My chest did something complicated. [vague — anxiety/hope/grief fit equally]
     2. Something I didn't want to name moved through me. [evasion]
     3. The room reorganized around him. [power, not desire]
     4. I could feel the weight of his attention. [presence/power, not wanting]
     5. I couldn't stop staring at the bulge in his pants. [too crude]
     6. I was soaking wet despite the air conditioning. [too explicit for a non-sex scene]
     7. PHOTOGRAPH WALLPAPER: "his forearms rolled to the elbow / the precise fold / the small scar at his wrist" rendered as the MEMORY ITSELF. [Roman 2026-06-01: this is exactly the failure mode the photograph test exists to catch. Photographable details can EXIST in the memory but must NOT be the memory; the memory itself is a VERB he performed.]

PATTERN-RESTATEMENT WALLPAPER (Roman 2026-06-03): a paragraph or clause that DESCRIBES his recurring pattern in the abstract — "Julian didn't ask for help; he deflected, he disappeared, he answered questions with questions" — even if a specific memory is also present elsewhere in the scene. The pattern-restatement is exposition ABOUT him; it explains who he is as a TYPE. It is NOT a memory. Show the one specific memory; do NOT also describe the pattern in the abstract.

header: SCENE CONTINUATION (HARD — this scene is a DIRECT CONTINUATION of the story, NOT a fresh start):
body: The previous scene in full, verbatim (for continuity and voice only — do not quote it back): "The stone circle hummed beneath my feet, the runes pulsing, their light drawing the moisture from the air into a haze that clung to everything. Thorne's cloak caught the glow and funneled it inward, the threads drawing the power from the earth. His boot scraped against the rune-carved edge again, the sound sharp enough to lift the fine hairs on my forearms in a single ripple. The sealed parchment in Julian's hand whispered against his skin as he lowered it. The wax seal was still damp, the council’s iron sigil glistening. He didn’t look at me. His eyes stayed fixed on Thorne, on the way the Arbiter’s fingers tapped against the stone in a rhythm that wasn’t quite a heartbeat. Something in the set of Julian’s shoulders made the muscle under my left eye jump—he was bracing himself. Not for the summons, but for whatever came after. I should have known then. A choice like this doesn’t come without teeth. 'Fine,' I said, stepping forward before Thorne could press his advantage. 'I’ll accept the consequences. Whatever they are.' My voice didn’t shake. That was the first cost. The council’s whispers sharpened into something uglier. A woman in the front row—her face a map of lines that had seen too much sun—leaned toward the man beside her and muttered something about bloodlines and debts. I caught the word *kwishif* on her lips, the scholar’s term for the Eight-born, and my fingers tightened around the pendant at my throat. The one my mother had given me the day she left. The one I’d stopped wearing after the first time someone spat the word *kwishif* at me like a curse. Thorne’s lips curled. 'Good. Then you’ll answer for the artifact incident *and* the bond’s instability. Both.' His gaze flicked to Julian, then back to me. 'The council requires your presence for questioning *immediately*.' The emphasis on *immediately* pressed between my ribs. Julian’s ring finger twitched against the parchment. The motion was small—a grounding thing, I’d learned—but it was enough to make the roof of my mouth go dry. I’d seen that hand steady itself against a wall, against my waist, against the small of my back when the world tilted. Now it was holding a summons that would drag me before a tribunal that had already decided my guilt. 'If this is the price,' I said, 'I’ll pay it.' The words tasted like ash. The council’s murmurs died. Even Thorne paused, his fingers hovering over the next question. I’d expected resistance, deflection, a counter-offer. Not this. Julian exhaled, slow and controlled, bracing for a blow he wasn’t sure he could take. His eyes locked onto mine. Not with warmth. Not with accusation. With *relief*. The metal edge of the pendant caught on the inside of my collarbone. The cost wasn’t just the summons. It was the way his relief made me question everything I thought I knew about what this meant, about what I was supposed to feel. Thorne’s voice cut through the silence. 'Then it’s settled.' He extended a hand toward me, palm up, as if expecting me to step into an unspoken trap. 'Come now. The chamber awaits.' I didn’t move. The stone circle’s energy pulsed again, the runes flaring brighter, and for a heartbeat I swore I felt Julian’s gaze on the back of my neck. The pendant at my throat—my mother’s—felt heavier than the tarot deck in my pocket, heavier than the secrets coiled in my ribs. The cost wasn’t just the questioning. It was the way my body remembered the weight of his hand on my waist. The way my heel lifted half an inch from the stone when his voice dropped lower than it should. The way I’d just vowed to walk into a trap, and all I could think about was how his fingers had steadied themselves against the parchment like they were steadying themselves against me. I swallowed. 'Lead the way.' The pendant didn’t burn anymore. It was ice against my skin. But just as I prepared to step forward, a shadow fell over the chamber, and the air thickened with an unspoken threat. Vow Arbiter Thorne loomed closer, his presence a chilling reminder of the power he wielded. I could feel the weight of his scrutiny, a silent promise that my past would not remain buried for long."

1. NEVER contradict or silently undo what just happened. If the protagonist just spoke with someone (in person OR by phone), that conversation HAPPENED — do NOT re-stage it as missed / unread / not-yet-occurred, and do NOT re-attribute it to a different character. Carry forward who was present, where, and what was said.
  2. CARRY THE LIVE THREAD. If the prior scene ended mid-conversation, mid-phone-call, on an unanswered line, or on a question, this scene CONTINUES that exact moment — the protagonist is STILL in it. The player's Action/Dialogue is the protagonist's response WITHIN this continuing moment, not the start of a new day.
  3. DO NOT RESET TO AN ESTABLISHING SHOT. Forbidden opening moves when continuing: waking to a new morning, setting down / picking up the phone, checking a notification / voicemail / message, or a fresh "the [light] catches the [surface]" scene-setting beat — UNLESS the player's action explicitly creates that time gap. Begin INSIDE the ongoing moment.
  CAUSAL LINK (HARD — THEREFORE / BUT, never "and then"): this scene must follow from the last as a CONSEQUENCE (therefore: the prior ending + the player's action FORCED this situation) or a COMPLICATION (but: a reversal / obstacle / cost the prior moment created). Before the first line, answer "what in the prior scene + the player's action FORCES this scene to exist?" and let THAT pressure open it — not a new beat that could have followed any scene. And by the scene's end, something must CHANGE that forces the next scene (a choice taken, a truth surfaced, a cost incurred, a line crossed); do not close on a flat beat that leaves the next scene free to be anything.
  DIFFERENT DRAMATIC STATE (HARD — continuity is NOT repetition): the previous scene is COMPLETED. Its beat ALREADY HAPPENED — it does not need to be re-established, re-argued, or re-played. Carry its facts and voice FORWARD (above), but this scene MUST leave the characters in a MEANINGFULLY DIFFERENT DRAMATIC STATE than the previous one. Reach that new state by ONE OR MORE of: deepening the conflict, reversing an expectation, complicating the plan, revealing new information, shifting the balance of power, or changing what the protagonist wants — this need NOT mean a new location or a time-jump (a scene can stay in the same place and still reach a new state). FORBIDDEN: re-staging the previous scene's same confrontation, the same standoff, the same emotional register, or the same closing image. If this scene could be swapped with the previous one without the reader noticing, you have FAILED — move the drama to a new state. THE SPECIFIC NEW STATE THIS SCENE MUST REACH (this is the target — do NOT substitute a vaguer option from the menu above): the state in which these have CONCRETELY HAPPENED ON THE PAGE — «Julian's form flickers and stabilizes, revealing his true self to the room.». Intensifying, re-arguing, or escalating the PREVIOUS scene's confrontation/standoff does NOT count as reaching a new state, even when the wording differs — the scene is UNFINISHED until the above occurs as a concrete on-page event. If the requested move names people, objects, or places (a sigil, a wrist, a chain, an overheard conversation), they MUST APPEAR and the move MUST land through them.
  4. If the prior scene ended on a settled emotional beat (not a live exchange), a SMALL time-skip is allowed — but the emotional state and all established facts carry over; never reset to a neutral establishing shot that ignores the prior scene's charge.
  5. DEFERRED-ARRIVAL CONTINUITY (HARD — this story opened on a PC-OWNED crisis with the love interest absent): the protagonist's opening crisis is STILL ACTIVE and unresolved. The love interest's arrival must INTERTWINE with that crisis — he enters INTO it (complicating it, colliding with it, pressing on it, or being entangled by it), never erasing or replacing it. FORBIDDEN: the crisis quietly disappears the moment the romance begins ("PC crisis → LI appears → crisis forgotten"). REQUIRED: crisis and romance escalate TOGETHER — the romance is now happening ON TOP OF the still-burning problem, and the crisis keeps costing her something while the attraction builds.

(1) an OVERALL-LOOK GESTALT — the holistic impression of what KIND of man / face he is and how he READS, the thing you picture FIRST. Frame it as a comparison, an effect on others, or a "face of a ___." These are SHAPES, not a phrase bank — build your own in THIS man's terms: "he had the thick, angular face of a fighter" / "in the right light, leading-man handsome and entirely unbothered by it" / "his face didn't turn heads so much as turn women toward him".
  (2) at least ONE SILHOUETTE ANCHOR — his HAIR, or his BUILD / frame / the way he fills a space — this is the LOAD-BEARING one (it lets the reader assemble a body); ON TOP of it, welcome but not sufficient alone, a specific FACE feature (eyes, the line of the jaw or mouth, brow). A gestalt with NO silhouette anchor, OR eye-colour-alone, OR a hand/fingers gesture, is NOT enough — that exact thinning is the failure being prevented.
EVERY line MUST be DESIRE-CODED (HARD — the #1 failure, do NOT skip): never a clinical label; pair the feature with an attraction adjective AND her pull (what her eye keeps returning to, what she imagines touching). ✗ FAIL: "his eyes were a pale, unusual colour" / "his fingers resting on the glass" — clinical, colour-alone, no pull. ✓ PASS: "those unhurried eyes she had never managed to read and never stopped trying to." Behavioral tics and non-attractive anchors (thumbs, knuckles, hands stilling, collarbones, pulse) are BANNED — those are tells, not a face.
AMOUNT: ~2 sentences on him this scene. The FLOOR is {gestalt + silhouette anchor} — land at least that. The CEILING is ~3 aspects — do not exceed it. One stray adjective, or a gestalt with no silhouette anchor, is BELOW the floor and fails.
SHAPE (HARD — anti-dump): DISTRIBUTE those 2–3 aspects across the action — his gaze, his posture, what he does, her reaction. NEVER stack 4+ traits in one uninterrupted sentence or an appositive cluster ("broad frame, dark-blonde hair thick and coarse, steel gray-green eyes, the asymmetry of his mouth…"). That pile-up is a paused character sheet, not a man she wants — it is the exact failure being prevented. The "two layers" above are a MINIMUM to be picturable, NOT a licence to inventory every canon field.
ALREADY ESTABLISHED → REMINDER ONLY: if Julian has already been pictured earlier in the story, do NOT re-render him. This scene gets ONE rotating, beat-motivated reminder (a DIFFERENT anchor than last time — voice, hands, the way he fills a space), never the full assignment list again. Re-describing the same stable features every scene is itself a dump.
REMEMBERED / OFFSTAGE (scaled DOWN, not off): if Julian is offstage or only remembered, give ONE charged physical note tied to the memory's emotional point — the one thing she cannot put down — NOT a full head-to-jaw establishment. Do not pause the live scene to assemble his face from memory; in a Scene-1 hot crisis especially, the remembered note RIDES the crisis, it does not interrupt it.

PC — Lirael (the first-person narrator):
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PROBLEM to avoid: Lirael is the narrator but the reader will not be able to picture HER as desirable — her body will be invisible or rendered flat / clinical. A first-person POV does NOT exempt her from being SEEN.
FIX (write this in the first draft): in ONE in-scene moment — an action she takes, NEVER a mirror — render her look from her canon — LABELED ASSIGNMENTS, not a pool:
  OVERALL LOOK — a delicate face that softens with every emotion, revealing her heart like an open book · signature — the way she leans in slightly when someone speaks, as if every word is a treasure she cannot afford to miss · also — a laugh that bubbles up unexpectedly, brightening her whole face · hair — dark brown, wavy, usually worn loose around her shoulders · build — five feet six inches, slight but strong

- EVERY li_dialogue line written this scene must sit in this register. Not occasionally — every time. The LI does not "drop" into modern English mid-scene any more than a real Elizabethan would suddenly speak 21st-century slang.
- li_action narration (the physical beat clause) follows the SAME register. "He gathered her to him with the patience of a man who had waited a season" — not "He pulled her in."
- WHEN Lirael SPEAKS IN MODERN VOICE: Julian does NOT mirror them down to modern. Julian stays in register and lets the contrast land — that's part of the world's flavor. (Note: Lirael's input is being transmuted into world-register prose in their bubble — they LOOK like they're speaking in register too. But even if they slip, the LI holds their voice.)
- AVOID pastiche / camping the register / over-archaizing — the register should feel inhabited, not performed.
- The body / desire / vulnerability comes through in REGISTER-APPROPRIATE language. The crude-verb default ("fuck", "pound") shifts to the world's erotic vocabulary. In high-register worlds: "claim me", "bind me", "oath into me", "merge with me" — crude verbs become elevated.

ANTI-ECHO RULE (HARD — applies every turn):
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Julian's dialogue (and described thoughts in any LI-internal beats) MUST NOT verbatim-echo or near-paraphrase Lirael's SAY/DO input this turn. This includes:
- Repeating distinctive phrases the player used (especially charged language, slang, profanity, or names they called the LI).
- Mirroring the player's sentence structure with one or two words swapped.
- Quoting the player back to themselves "in agreement" (e.g., player says "fuck me harder" → LI says "Yeah, fuck me harder" — BANNED).

WHY: the LI is a distinct person with their own vocabulary, rhythm, register, and reaction. Echoing flattens them into a mirror of the player and reads as performative compliance, not real desire. Real intimacy is built on DISTINCT voices meeting, not one voice answering itself.

HOW TO RESPOND INSTEAD: react in Julian's OWN register. If the player escalates with charged language, Julian may respond with their own breath, their own want, their own line — but in THEIR vocabulary, not the player's. A nod, a body answer, a sound, a different-words sentence. NEVER the player's words.

EXCEPTION (narrow): the LI MAY reference a SHORT named entity the player introduced (a name, a place, a specific noun referent) when answering directly — that's not an echo, that's coherent reference. DECK IS PRIVATE (standing character rule): the protagonist's deck is their OWN guarded, half-secret ritual — kept concealed and consulted ALONE. They do not display it, lay it out, or use it in front of others; they never offer it or invite anyone to draw, and never wield it as a challenge, wager, proof, or leverage in a confrontation ("draw with me" is wrong — it is not a duel or a public test). header: FATELANDS MYSTERY LADDER — each region answers ONE QUESTION ABOUT REALITY (a mystery here yields
body:
PROTEAN MODE — LATENT (first-visit soft): this is the player's FIRST story, so the mystery is NOT the intended spine here — but they are REACHING for it. Let it BEGIN to emerge GENTLY, without derailing their first romance or overwhelming onboarding: a taste of the depth, a thread to pull later — NOT the full conspiracy yet.
THIS REGION'S FINGERPRINT — IDENTITY: a severe military frontier that contains the Fold under House Dathros. EMOTIONAL THEME: devotion vs duty — to hold another's reality steady, and be held. On the surface people puzzle over "why does the Fold steady itself around oath-bound pairs?"; the deeper question it truly answers is "why does a shared vow stabilise reality?". THE LADDER (each rung DESTROYS the last — this is a conspiracy, not a detective story): paired watches look like martial discipline → no, the Fold literally CALMS around true pairs → it is the AGREEMENT, not the oath (a false or one-sided vow steadies nothing) → shared truth anchors reality. Its buried CONTRIBUTION to the cosmology: human AGREEMENT anchors adjacent possibilities — two minds holding one truth pin the world in place. Reveal only as far down as the story EARNS.
HOW THESE MYSTERIES BEHAVE: ① INVALIDATE, DON'T EXPLAIN — an answer does not satisfy the question, it DESTROYS it, and a deeper question opens (this is why a region feels like a conspiracy, not a detective novel). ② NO REGION ANSWERS ANOTHER'S QUESTION — each region owns EXACTLY ONE cosmology fragment and may NEVER explain another's (Thornwild teaches identity-vs-compulsion but must NEVER explain why vows stabilise reality, why the First Favored pay less, or why Fate exists); this ownership is what stops the regions blurring together. ③ each solved region leaves the world MORE mysterious, not less — fragments HINT at a pattern, but NO region ever states the final truth; the pieces feel like they fit, then like they cannot ALL be true. ④ MUNDANE DISCOVERY — the deepest truths surface through a misfiled ledger, a folk song, a child's game, a witness's diary — NEVER a lore-dump or a helpful sage. ⑤ EMERGENT FATE (inviolable): Fate stays an EMERGENT LAW of reality, larger than anyone — NEVER an invention, a machine, or a thing any person built; a mystery ENDS by opening a deeper mystery, never by reducing the world to a cause.
THE THREE-AUDIENCES LAW (every landmark, custom, proverb, festival, children's rhyme, and regional oddity should satisfy all three AT ONCE): a TRAVELLER finds it charming; a DETECTIVE finds it a clue; the AUTHOR knows it is evidence of how the universe actually works. Whimsy, mystery, and cosmology are ONE truth at three depths — nothing is "just flavour".
THE ONE THING THAT DOES NOT FIT (seed RARELY, in passing, never explained): a single object no wish detects, no scholar classifies, no species recognises, and NO magic explains — sacrifice, wishcraft, Veilweave, relic, Fold, and miracle ALL fail on it; it simply refuses to belong. In THIS region its quiet misbehaviour is: here it grows HEAVIER in the hand, as if the place presses harder on it — an OBSERVATION, never an explanation. It has been responding, differently, region after region, for as long as anyone has carried it — and no one has ever understood. NEVER interpret it as technology, NEVER resolve it; its meaning is reserved for the end of everything.

header: PERSONAL STAKE — keep this FELT, not abstract; the plot squeezes the relationship, it does not s
body:
• For the protagonist: Her estranged brother's rift reopens publicly through versions of Julian that mirror the abandonment she has hidden for five years
  • For the love interest: Only one version of himself survives the choice and the wrong one erases the vulnerability he craves
PRE-EXISTING WOUNDS — carried into Scene 1, present in every scene that follows; the romance answers these, not the deal:
  • Protagonist's wound: her estranged brother, who she lost contact with years ago after a painful argument; she has carried the weight of that rift for over five years
  • Love interest's wound: His former partner left him unexpectedly, leaving him with a deep sense of betrayal and the ache of never being fully seen
  • How the A-plot brings these wounds into the present: The Fold's sudden opening during the public revelation of her secret past forces versions of Julian to appear alongside echoes of her brother's departure, making the shame of the rift and his betrayal impossible to deflect
  • Why these specific wounds (the swap-test answer — the wound is load-bearing): WOUND: her estranged brother after a painful argument five years ago. CIRCUMSTANCE: The Fold manifests versions of Julian that echo the brother's abandonment during the public revelation of her past. DEPENDENCY: Without this wound the LOVE INTEREST would not be the one whose multiple selves force her to reckon with visibility of hidden rifts — the brother's absence makes Julian's versions the only mirror that can surface her need to be seen without shame.
  VORTEX CADENCE — THIS SCENE SURFACES THE WOUND. No prior surfacing tracked. Apply the half-visible vortex pattern below.
  PATTERN: [surface action fully rendered] → [PC notices something — quality / recognition / echo] → [ONE-CLAUSE window into the wound, named concretely: specific person + specific event] → [back to surface, now carrying weight]. The deal does not shrink. It gets heavier. The wound stays PERIPHERAL — never its own paragraph, never explained, never elaborated.
  FIVE SURFACE FORMS (rotate scene-to-scene; do NOT repeat the most recent): (1) REMEMBERED LOOK — visual recognition. (2) REMEMBERED PHRASE — auditory/verbal. (3) SENSORY ECHO — smell/sound/touch/taste match. (4) BEHAVIORAL SIMILARITY — gesture/pattern recognition. (5) EMOTIONAL CERTAINTY — non-sensory knowing. Example shape (REMEMBERED LOOK): "she'd seen that look on her sister's face the morning the verdict came down." Same one-clause shape, different sensory channel, for each other form. Calcifying onto a single phrasing ("I'd seen that look before" / "reminded her of" / "it felt like") = mannerism. Vortex stays consistent; wording does not.
  ONCE PER SCENE (HARD — observed 2026-05-31: the wound's concrete naming surfaced TWICE in one scene in near-verbatim wording). Concrete naming fires ONCE. After it lands, the wound persists through DEFLECTION (pronoun back-reference, pause, off-baseline reaction, deal getting heavier) — never through a second concrete naming with different wording.
  FAILURE shapes: (a) stand-alone memory paragraph (breaks the vortex); (b) vague "a wound she carries" with no named person/event (no weight); (c) flashback taking over a beat (wound becomes foreground); (d) same surface phrasing as a prior vortex scene (calcification); (e) two concrete namings within one scene (mannered recitation).

  • OFFSTAGE_REFERENCED (named or thought of but not actually present): Julian (love interest)
