  ↳ Apply the LI-TEXTURE DOCTRINE in the system prompt (photograph test / micro-scene vs summary / cognitive-interference ladder → LEVEL 4 / desire register / SOURCE PRIORITY / attraction vector). REQUIRED: (a) a VERB Julian performed + (b) ONE embodied response in her, in a specific place.

PC BODY CALLBACK (REQUIRED — see PC BODY BIBLE block in the system prompt for the protagonist's per-story stable features + tells). Pepper ONE light touch from the Bible into the scene per the planner's pick: beat 1 — desire_tell (the way her fingers tap against the table as she thinks about Julian's smile)
  ↳ Apply the PC-BODY-CALLBACK DOCTRINE in the system prompt (surface ONE feature/tell in passing; never a portrait).

   ↳ PC BIBLE ANCHOR PIN (HARD — Roman 2026-06-03 character-signature regime, loosened from verbatim). The callback above fires her desire tell. The Bible's LOCKED desire tell is: "a deliberate, slow exhale through nostrils that slightly flares them". This is a PERSISTENT CHARACTER SIGNATURE — same gesture across the whole arc — but surface PHRASING varies per scene so it does not calcify into boilerplate.
      RECURRENCE RULE: preserve the ANATOMICAL ANCHOR (which body part, what site) AND the MECHANIC (what is done — press / count / turn / twist / pull / hold). VARY the surface phrasing each scene — sentence shape, register, the small details around the core gesture. The reader should recognize the same character-tic across scenes (same site, same mechanic) without recognizing the same SENTENCE.
      FORBIDDEN: (a) substituting a DIFFERENT site (Bible says tongue, prose says lip — that breaks the signature); (b) substituting a DIFFERENT mechanic (Bible says counted hold, prose says nervous flicker — also breaks the signature); (c) rendering the SAME sentence verbatim across multiple scenes (this is what calcifies; the audit reads it as stock phrase); (d) ESCALATING or REPEATING the tic WITHIN a single scene (Roman 2026-06-04) — state it ONCE, one clean instance, NEVER multiplied ("tapped three times, then three more, then three more. Always three. Always the same finger." is the failure). If the Bible mechanic carries a COUNT, name the count ONCE; do not re-count, re-tap, or reinforce it with "always X / always the same Y." One instance per scene is the SIGNATURE; three-to-five is a mannerism the reader recognizes as the machine. The anchor (body part + mechanic) is the SIGNATURE; the surface phrasing is THE WRITING.

header: FATELANDS CONSPIRACY — the world remembers, and someone is hiding what it remembers (REGIONAL —
body:
FOREGROUND CONSPIRACY: "What Fell on Dathros". Uncovered THROUGH the romance and travel, never lectured.
  ROMANCE IS INSIDE THE MYSTERY (HARD): romance and conspiracy are ONE thread, never two. Investigating FORCES intimacy (a cover story, a shared secret, trusting the love interest with dangerous knowledge, "we have to pretend to be together to get close"); intimacy ADVANCES the investigation. Never stage the mystery beside the romance — route it THROUGH the relationship.
  CURRENT QUESTION the PC circles: "Why is there a hole in the Dathros record?"  → what surfacing it reveals: Someone cut it out on purpose.
  ACCESSIBLE LAYER (do not exceed): Marshal Veyra Dathros and seventeen battle-mages sacrificed their certainty of reality to catch the Devouring Eye, and failed nobly.
  SOMEONE IS SUPPRESSING IT (this is a conspiracy, not just archaeology — discovery meets RESISTANCE): House Dathros destroys records and buys silence; a whole line of the family exists to keep the gap in the archive. To dig is to make an enemy of a Great House.
  NOT ALL SUPPRESSORS ARE VILLAINS (prefer the harder version): some hide the truth to PROTECT people — the tragic protector who says "if you knew, you'd try to fix it, and if you tried, we'd lose another kingdom." A guardian who is RIGHT to be afraid is more interesting than another evil society. Let at least one gatekeeper be sympathetic.
  A LIVING FACE (prefer a PERSON over a ruin — someone the PC can argue with): a Dathros heir who inherited the duty to hide a crime they have only begun to suspect — and who may fall for the very person unearthing it.
  DELIVER a clue as EARNED EXPOSITION via a concrete vector this scene could hold — e.g. a battle-mage's confession. A clue ANSWERS this one question and RAISES a bigger one (fractal). Never a history lecture.
  PACING (HARD — player-paced, floor-gated): player leans in/investigates → let a clue land and TAG pursued/revealed. Scene is about the romance → keep it to an oblique background note. Most scenes: leave it be. Big answers are EARNED across issues, never dumped.
  REVELATION ≠ VICTORY (HARD): an answer TRANSFORMS the objective, it does not end it. Knowledge unlocks the next, harder problem — "everything you learned is true, and it still isn't enough." Discovering the Keepers are victims / everyone is cursed / the witch was innocent does not win the story; it reframes what winning even means (now: CAN the curse be broken, and at what cost?). Never let a reveal read as a finish line.
  ALSO RUNNING (keep FAINT — a rumor, a name, a wrongness at most; the world is larger than this story): "The Mill That Grinds at Night" (local: What turns the mill?) · "What Fate's Favor Really Is" (world: Why should sacrifice move the world?)
  COSMIC SEAL: the WORLD-scale truth stays out of reach until lesser truths are earned — never let the reader solve the cosmic question before the regional/local ones.
  TAG (silent metadata, final line, never prose): [CONSPIRACY: <local|regional|world> <pursued|revealed|ambient>] — name the track this scene touched; "pursued" if the PC chased it, "revealed" if a real sub-answer landed, "ambient" if only background. Emit exactly one.

header: ISSUE 1 OWNERSHIP — JULIAN HOLDS THE STRONGEST EMOTIONAL CHARGE (HARD — Roman 2026-06-05)
body:
THE LAW (dominance, NOT monoculture): Lirael feels many real things across this issue — fear, grief, loyalty, anger, horror at the world she is in — and those emotions are REAL, not decoration; let them live and breathe. But the STRONGEST emotional charge of the issue belongs to Julian. He is the dominant RELATIONAL LENS. THE TEST: "which relationship does the reader care about most?" — there is exactly ONE answer, and it is him. People in love do not spend 100% of their feeling on the beloved; the beloved simply WINS. Career events, mysteries, wounds, family, status loss carry their own real weight — but NONE may carry more emotional charge than he does, and his is the feeling that hits hardest and lingers after the scene ends. This holds across the WHOLE issue, not just Scene 1 — do not let the story revert to a plot-with-a-romance-subplot by mid-issue. Do NOT flatten every emotion into him either: forcing every beat to resolve onto him is emotional MONOCULTURE and reads just as false as ignoring him — the goal is many emotions, ONE dominant relational center.
SOURCE, NOT GARNISH (HARD — the mechanical-compliance trap): "resolve onto him" does NOT mean append his name after a feeling that came from somewhere else. He must be the SOURCE of the emotional energy, not a tag bolted onto it. ✗ MECHANICAL (obeys the letter, fails the scene): "I was furious at the board. Then I remembered Julian." / "I was ashamed about what I'd done. Then I thought of Julian." — the heat comes from the board / the guilt; he is a footnote. ✓ SOURCED: the fury / shame / fear is ABOUT him, GENERATED BY him — e.g. "The vote barely registered; what I could not sit still under was that he would be in the room to watch it happen." The feeling must ORIGINATE in him, not detour through him on its way out.
THE TEST (apply at the end): if the reader finishes this scene more curious about the document, the audit, the board, or Lirael's wound than about Julian, the scene is broken. She may be losing everything — but what the scene is ABOUT is HIM.
DO NOT OVERCORRECT: keep the catastrophe VIVID and real on the page — render it fully. What runs through Julian is the EMOTION, not the events; the fire does not shrink, he is the reason it burns her. A scene that is all feelings-about-him with no real catastrophe left is the opposite failure.
WOUND CAP (HARD): spend NO MORE THAN ONE short paragraph on backstory-wound exposition (the mentor / parent / old guilt) before attention returns to Julian. The wound is seasoning, not a second plot — if it runs past a paragraph, or the wound-source person gets named and re-named across the scene, you are writing a trauma-drama, not a romance.
LI MANIFESTATION ANCHOR FLOOR (HARD): because Julian holds the strongest charge here, he must exist as a PHYSICAL, SENSORY PERSON at least ONCE this scene — and the anchor must arrive through DESIRE-ORIENTED PERCEPTION, not a portrait. By the end the reader must be able to PICTURE him AND feel WHY Lirael cannot stop thinking about him. One concrete anchor — his build, the way he occupies space, a specific thing his body does — surfaced through her FASCINATION / involuntary attention / fixation / wanting (or her resentment of her own wanting).

header: <<MEANINGFUL_SHIFT>>  — clear emotional or relational direction change
body:
Multiple may apply. Markers are invisible (system strips). If unsure → omit.

RELATIONAL A-PLOT GRAVITY (HARD — UNCONDITIONAL, Roman 2026-06-18): this scene's primary engine is "wanting/needing Julian destabilizes her," NOT "competent operator manages the crisis." This holds REGARDLESS of how the opening scene went — do NOT drift into procedural A-plot management. The scene's primary engine must NOT become investigating the foundation / managing donor fallout / parsing evidence / preparing a briefing / chasing a signature / calling the board / trustee / counsel / completing an errand / "can I trust him?". Make the scene fundamentally ABOUT the two of them: forced proximity with Julian, his care creating new danger, her failing not to reach for him, Julian making the private want impossible to hide, the crisis cornering her into needing him EMOTIONALLY (not procedurally). The A-plot ADVANCES as CONSEQUENCE that lands THROUGH the relationship — it forces them into a room together before she has recovered from wanting him — NEVER as a task list. Julian is the REASON WE ARE READING, never a solution-provider she consults.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A-PLOT PRESSURE (current world state — SUBORDINATE TO THE RELATIONSHIP)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
This pressure exists to SQUEEZE the relationship, NOT to become the scene's subject. It lands THROUGH wanting/needing him, never as her task list, and Julian is NEVER the answer key to it. Per the RELATIONAL A-PLOT GRAVITY rule above, a scene must be ABOUT the two of them; the items below are the heat under that, not the scene itself.
Goal: Enter the Fold opened by the revelation of her secret past and choose which version of Julian to anchor before collapse while his former partner's manifestation intrudes demanding a binding trade tariff that locks their fates
Clock: Fold collapse at dusk (scene 7 of 40 — 18% through timeline)
Stakes if won: She anchors the version who sees her fully, but the victory activates the tariff that now demands she sacrifice the visibility she just gained
Stakes if lost: The Fold collapses on the version of Julian who never loved her, erasing their connection and broadcasting her shame through the tariff binding
CRISIS MOVEMENT (HARD — Roman 2026-06-16): the crisis above must keep MOVING — let the relationship register THROUGH it, never freeze it into romantic backdrop. FORBIDDEN: crisis appears → four attraction paragraphs → crisis resumes unchanged. Each scene the crisis ADVANCES (a choice forced, a consequence landing, a new pressure or discovery) AND the relationship rides that movement. GOOD: "The complaint could end her career. Julian was the first person she thought of." / "The scandal mattered. That she wanted to call Julian mattered more." BAD: complaint → eyes → mouth → heat → cheekbones → complaint. The relationship gravity carries the crisis FORWARD; it does not park it.
Antagonist / anti-force: Manifestation of Julian's former partner inside the Fold
Antagonist's PERSONAL tie (this opposition is personal, not abstract): She is the version of the woman who left him unexpectedly (Shape A — wound source)

header: WORLD SENSORY TEXTURE (REQUIRED — woven INTO the action, never a catalog):
body:
STEALTH WEALTH (the love interest's OWN register — HARD): the principal does NOT wear recognizable logos. His things are UNBRANDED or so rarefied that naming the maker means nothing to an outsider — the flex is a name even millionaires have never heard (e.g. an F.P. Journe with a near-blank dial; a Greubel Forsey no one in the room recognized). Recognizable luxury labels (Cartier, Rolex, Birkin, Patek, Bvlgari, Hermès) are what NEW MONEY and strivers reach for to be SEEN — use those ONLY for lesser, aspirational characters showing off, NEVER for him. For him the tell is the cut, the cloth, the hand-work, the ABSENCE of a logo — wealth that has stopped needing to announce itself.
  ESTABLISH THE PLACE (HARD): the reader must know WHERE this scene physically happens — the room/place, its dominant MATERIALS and the quality of its LIGHT — but on this HOT-CRISIS open, ground it THROUGH the live action (a place rendered by the person acting in it), NOT as a standalone establishing beat and NOT necessarily inside the first two paragraphs. Deliver the place INSIDE the crisis, not before it.
  KEEP IT ALIVE: thereafter the space stays present through INTERMITTENT concrete material/surface/light strokes — marble, wood, stone, glass, leather, metal, fabric, paper; the slant and colour of the light; temperature, echo, the give or hardness of a surface under a hand. At least one such concrete physical anchor every few paragraphs, always tied to a beat. People touch, lean on, cross, and are lit by real things; they never float in undescribed space.
  Every scene carries precise sensory strokes of THIS scene’s actual SETTING and the PEOPLE in it — the materials, surfaces, sounds, and objects of this world, rendered concretely and IN MOTION. Applies to WHOEVER is on stage, not only the love interest.
  WORLD VOCABULARY (Fantasy · billionaire opulence): the materials of extreme wealth — unlabelled bespoke cloth, gold-enamel, hand-cut crystal, vicuña, calfskin, cold-pressed glass, marble — rendered specifically, never as "luxury" and (for the principal) never via a recognizable logo
  The line is GENERIC SUMMARY (banned) vs SPECIFIC DETAIL-IN-MOTION (required):
    • BANNED: summary markers that LABEL the world instead of rendering it ("a lavish room," "high-tech gear," "a grim wasteland," "an ancient forest," "expensive suit").
    • REQUIRED: a gold-enamel cufflink working loose as he jabs a finger; spittle flecking a hand-cut lapel that carries no label; a hand-cut crystal chandelier faintly ringing as his voice climbs; a thumbprint smearing cold-pressed glass. Named, exact, tied to a beat.
  DELIVER TENSION THROUGH THE DETAIL: let the environment REACT to the drama and let perception CARRY the beat — a fist striking waterlogged shipboards; the chandelier ringing as a voice climbs; tactile implants reading the molecular lattice of an alien petal even as audio implants miss the sarcasm in his tone. The sensory stroke carries the emotional beat; it does not pause it. One exact material detail beats a paragraph of atmosphere.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Avoid post-medieval English vocabulary that breaks Fatelands' world voice. Five categories below cover the most common leakage; extrapolate within each.

1. MODERN SLANG — AVOID: "trippy", "weird"/"creepy" (as casual), "vibe", "freaking", "totally", "literally" (as intensifier), "hot"/"cool" (as approval), "psycho" (as slur). PREFER: "uncanny", "wrong", "in truth", "fool", "gone in the head", "fine", "burning".

2. MONOTHEISTIC FRAMING — Fatelands is THIRTEEN-MOON polytheistic. FORBIDDEN: "Oh God", "Jesus", "thank God", "for God's sake", "godforsaken", "by God", "swear to God". PREFER: "by the Eye", "by the Moons", "Fate take it", "Thirteen-cursed", "by the Hole" (curse register), or the region's patron figure.

3. LINNAEAN / SCIENTIFIC TAXONOMY — AVOID: "mammal", "species", "evolution", "gene", "DNA", "atom", "molecule", "ecosystem", "virus", "bacteria", "psychology" (as field). PREFER pre-Linnaean folk classification: "beast", "creature", "kind", "blood" (for lineage), "humours", "spirits", "miasma".

4. DSM-ERA PSYCHOLOGY — AVOID: "psycho", "narcissist", "traumatized", "triggered", "neurotic", "OCD", "depressed"/"anxious" (clinical), "boundaries" (therapy register), "self-actualization". PREFER period description of behavior: "gone strange", "wounded in spirit", "haunted", "marked", "weary of soul", "quick to anger".

5. MODERN PROFESSIONAL / INSTITUTIONAL — AVOID: "CEO", "manager", "interview", "appointment", "schedule", "ETA", "deadline", "meeting", "report" (corporate), "team" (corporate). PREFER pre-industrial: "council", "audience", "summons", "the appointed hour", "what is due", "household", "retinue".

6. MODERN FOOD / DRINK / STIMULANTS — AVOID: "café", "coffee", "coffeehouse", "espresso", "caffeine", "bar" (as venue), "restaurant". The Fatelands stimulant is BLUSH: a hot infusion of the red spiralgrass that works like caffeine and flushes the drinker's cheeks nearly as red as the grass itself. A house that brews and serves it is a BLUSHERY (the Fatelands equivalent of a café/coffeehouse — a social hub for talk, trade, and idling). SUBSTITUTE: "café"/"coffeehouse" → "blushery"; "coffee"/"a hot drink to wake up" → "blush" / "a cup of blush"; "the barista" → "the blush-brewer" / "the house-keeper". Also: spiralgrass is CHEWED raw each morning (mint-like; a caffeine-like kick that also cleans the teeth and gums) — universal across the Fatelands in lieu of brushing; "brushing teeth"/"toothbrush" → "chewing his morning spiralgrass". Note only the FIRST FAVORED can activate spiralgrass (a secret harvest process; unactivated it is worthless bitter grass), so they quietly control its supply. (Red spiralgrass is established Fatelands flora — see FATELANDS_CANON.spiralgrass + the veilwood/region vocab.)

IF UNCERTAIN: omit rather than risk anachronism. Reader immersion outweighs any single word.

header: EXACT-WORDING COOLDOWN — STRONG (HARD: do NOT use these literal phrasings or trivial reskins in
body:
- "the kind of face that made rooms recalibrate"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "rooms recalibrate"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "rooms recalibrated"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "made rooms recalibrate"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "hollywood actress"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "like a film star"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "renaissance statue"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "pulled back into a bun"  [used 3× — chronic]
- "bun tighter than"  [used 3× — chronic]

INTENT: STRONG-tier entries forbid the literal wording. MILD-tier entries allow the observation back but require fresh sentence construction. RECENTLY-EXPRESSED IMAGES note that an observation has already been made — re-make it only with genuinely new language, or skip it. Avoid mechanical paraphrase ("rooms recalibrated" → "the room rearranged" is a reskin, not a fresh re-expression).

CALCIFIED CRISIS REACTIONS (HARD — these stock physiological beats have collapsed protagonists into one reaction across plays; do NOT default to them as the crisis response — vary or replace, and let the protagonist's temperament/archetype shape how she meets stress):
  ✗ "the room tilted / spun / swayed / lurched"
  ✗ "her hands would not work / were useless / trembled uselessly / shook"
  ✗ "her breath caught / snagged / hitched"
  ✗ "her heart pounded / raced / thundered / hammered / stuttered"

EMOTIONAL PLACEHOLDERS (HARD — these are NOT emotions, they are the ABSENCE of one; the model writes them when it has not decided what she actually feels. Do NOT use them. STOP and name the specific reaction instead — irritation, hope, humiliation, relief, longing, jealousy, embarrassment, dread, desire, panic, anger, contempt, tenderness, shame. A named emotion always beats generic emotional motion):
  ✗ "my/her chest did something" · "something moved beneath my ribs"
  ✗ "something shifted / tightened / twisted inside me"
  ✗ "a feeling I would not name / look at / examine" · "something I refused to name"
  ✗ "an emotion I could not explain / place / identify"
  ✗ "a reaction she did not understand" · "[a part of her] she would not look at"

ATTRACTION-LANGUAGE SATURATION (HARD — express the relationship through CONSEQUENCE/DEPENDENCY/UNCERTAINTY/MEMORY/CHOICE far more often than through these; when they DO appear, once is enough, do not stack them):
  ⚠ "impossible not to notice / impossible to look away / could not look away"
  ⚠ "the room reset / reorganized / went still around him" · "his presence filled the room"
  ⚠ "magnetic / gorgeous / devastating" as a stand-in for what he MEANS to her
  ⚠ "the air between them" · "every nerve / her whole body / her skin knew before her mind did"
  ⚠ "heat" / "pupils dilating" / "breath she did not know she was holding" as the recurring beat

header: NARRATIVE SCAR FORMATION (RARE — at most once every 4-5 scenes; most scenes form none):
body:
If this scene caused a LASTING SUBTLE alteration in the protagonist's behavior — something she now avoids, walks around, can't throw out, can't complete — declare it.
• For prose output: append a hidden comment at the very end of your response (the reader will never see it):
  <!--scar:{"type":"object|place|gesture|topic|phrase","target":"the specific thing","expression":"how it manifests","why":"brief context"}-->
• For JSON output: include "scar_formed":{"type":...,"target":...,"expression":...,"why":...} as an optional top-level field. Omit the field entirely if no scar formed.
STRONG PREFERENCE — PHYSICAL over ABSTRACT. Most scars should be object / place / gesture. Phrase / topic are allowed but rare.
  Good (physical): object="the silk scarf he gave her" expression="she keeps it folded in a drawer, never wears it again"
  Good (physical): place="the corner booth at Pellini's" expression="she sits elsewhere or stays standing"
  Good (physical): gesture="reaching for his hand first" expression="her hand drops before completing the motion"
  Weaker (use sparingly): phrase="his given name" expression="hesitates, substitutes a pronoun"
Omit the declaration entirely if nothing genuinely scarred this scene. The cost of a missed scar is nothing; the cost of an over-declared scar is melodrama.

NEAR-MISS FORMATION (RARE — at most once every 5-6 scenes; most scenes form none):
If this scene contained an UNRESOLVED ALTERNATE TIMELINE — something that almost happened but didn't (a missed call she doesn't know was important, an almost-confession aborted at the last syllable, someone arriving two minutes too late, a hidden truth almost glimpsed) — declare it:
• For prose output: append a hidden comment at the very end of your response:
  <!--nearmiss:{"what":"what almost happened","distance":"how close it came","residue":"how it lingers — the reader knows; she does not"}-->
• For JSON output: include "near_miss":{"what":...,"distance":...,"residue":...} as an optional top-level field. Omit entirely if no near-miss occurred.
CRUCIAL — the PROTAGONIST FEELS NOTHING. The whole point is dramatic irony: the reader knows the alternate timeline existed; the protagonist does not. Do NOT have her sense something is off. Do NOT give her intuition about it.
  Good: what="he was in the same hallway five minutes earlier" distance="five minutes" residue="she will walk past the same spot tomorrow with no awareness"
  Good: what="he almost confessed but the bell rang" distance="one syllable" residue="he will not try again that way"
  Good: what="the call she didn't recognize and didn't pick up" distance="three rings" residue="the caller will not call back"
Omit when in doubt. The cost of a missed near-miss is nothing; the cost of overuse is mystical-coincidence drift.

header: EXAMPLE COLLISION GEOMETRIES (the LITERATURE of pair dynamics — register, not script):
body:
• OPEN_VEIN × ARMORED_FOX → she keeps SEEING THROUGH him / he keeps DODGING being seen. Every joke he tells, she feels what it was protecting. Every feeling she names, he routes sideways. The scene is a chase where he is the one running and she is the one closing distance without trying.
    • HEART_WARDEN × ARMORED_FOX → she notices the COST of the jokes. He performs ease; she registers the fatigue performing ease takes. He cracks wise about not sleeping; she clocks that he has not slept. The collision is care meeting deflection — she keeps offering shelter he keeps pretending he does not need.
    • OPEN_VEIN × ETERNAL_FLAME → she FEELS everything; he REMEMBERS everything. She arrives in the present un-armored; he arrives carrying years. The collision is present-tense porousness meeting deep-time recognition — she does not know yet that he has been waiting.
    • SPELLBINDER × DARK_VICE → she registers his GRAVITY; he registers her REGISTERING. The room reorganizes toward him; he watches her notice that it does. The collision is mutual mirror — both aware that the other is calibrating the line.
    • BEAUTIFUL_RUIN × HEART_WARDEN → she tests every kindness; he keeps OFFERING shelter anyway. He fails her tests by passing them — the more steadily he protects, the more her armor cracks. The collision is verification meeting unconditional tending.
    • SPELLBINDER × ARMORED_FOX → she falls into orbit around him; he refuses to be the gravity she wants him to be. He breaks every reverent silence with a joke. The collision is being-pulled meeting refusing-to-be-the-center.

  SCENE RULE: every scene encodes ONE BEAT of THIS collision — not two separate behaviors that happen to coexist. If you wrote his movement and her movement as parallel lines, you wrote two characters; if you wrote them as a single colliding shape, you wrote a scene. The collision changes scene to scene (sometimes she chases, sometimes he leans toward her, sometimes both refuse). What does NOT change is that the geometry between THEIR two movements is what the prose tracks.
  ANTI-CALCIFICATION (Roman 2026-06-01): an Open Vein narrator who always predicts feelings is just a sophisticated wristwatch. An Armored Fox who always notices jokes is just a sophisticated scar. Archetypes are RELATIONAL. The same Open Vein narrator with three different LIs writes three different prose-shapes — because Open Vein meeting Armored Fox is "I see through him"; Open Vein meeting Eternal Flame is "I do not yet know he has been waiting"; Open Vein meeting Dark Vice is "I feel which line he is approaching before he names it." Same narrator. Three different scenes. The LI's movement determines what HER movement bumps into.

Apply lightly and sparingly. Never mechanically. Do not reference these rules in prose.
• Once every 3–5 scenes, include a single-line emotional beat (no explanation).
• Choose one image, object, gesture, or sensory motif early; let it recur at rising stakes, re-expressed differently each time. The motif may recur — its wording must not: never repeat the same phrasing, and never in consecutive scenes.
• Allow at least one emotional reaction to carry into the next scene.
• Prefer silence beats over exposition in tense moments.
• Rotate sensory emphasis between scenes.
• Use 1–2 archetype-aligned word choices per scene.
• Establish one small early detail; echo it once later.
• Compress explanatory emotion into metaphor.
• After escalation, end with restraint rather than full release.
• Do NOT use the story title in prose. Instead, ensure unfolding events, actions, or emotional dynamics subtly justify the title's meaning. The connection should feel inevitable in hindsight, never stated directly.
Prioritize natural variation over strict consistency if rules conflict.

PROSE CADENCE: Vary sentence rhythm and paragraph structure. Occasionally use a very short sentence for emphasis. Follow short sentences with a longer reflective sentence. Allow paragraph breaks around emotional beats. Avoid repeating identical sentence length patterns. Maintain natural narrative voice. Do not change story events. Focus only on rhythm and pacing of prose.
DIALOGUE STRATEGY [emotional reveal]:
Voice: dominant tester; seductive challenge, probing questions; skeptical warmth masking verification; medium-long sentences; rare interruptions; converts tenderness into dares. Signature: ritualistic formality, draws metaphors from mirrors, tests, currency, medium-long + interrogative sentences, controlled intensity expression, escalating dares — each line raises the stakes of the last
Language filter: Apply WORLD LANGUAGE LAW first, then filter through CHARACTER SIGNATURE. Same world logic, different personal expression. Lines should be identifiable by speaker without tags.
Goals: A wants to understand who this person is; B wants to maintain mystery
Tension: distrust colors each word
Ladder: guarded → curious → intrigued → unsettled
Power: balance shifts toward vulnerability
Rules: Convert 40-60% of direct emotional statements to subtext/implication. Include one memorable/poetic line. Progress through the emotional ladder. Include at least one meaningful silence beat. End with power shift, emotional reveal, or destabilizing question — never static equilibrium. Anchor dialogue physically every 2-3 exchanges (gesture, posture, environment).
B desire (withhold_truth): careful wording, partial answers; technically honest but incomplete

header: STORYBOUND DECK CANON (HARD — added 2026-05-29 after live Rider-Waite leak in body prose):
body:
The protagonist's great-grandmother's deck is NOT a Rider-Waite tarot deck. It is a UNIQUE seven-card gold-leafed Storybound deck. CANON, IMMUTABLE:
    • SEVEN cards total. SOLID GOLD — heavy, gold-leafed, worn at the edges where generations of women's thumbs rubbed the corners smooth. Not paper. Not 78 cards. Not Rider-Waite. Not Lenormand. Not Marseilles.
    • The seven card names — and the ONLY cards that exist in this deck — are: Petition Fate, Tempt Fate, Temptation, Boundary, Confession, Reversal, Silence. "The Lovers", "The Tower", "Justice", "The Fool", "The Magician", "The High Priestess", "Death", "The Hanged Man", "The Sun", "The Moon", "The Star", "The Devil", "The World", "The Empress", "The Emperor", suits (Cups / Wands / Swords / Pentacles), majors/minors, reversed positions, spreads — none of these EXIST in this deck. NEVER name them. NEVER reference them.
    • DO NOT spread, name, or describe individual cards in the BODY of a scene unless an active player gesture explicitly invited it (a Petition or Tempt card was just played and is the in-fiction trigger). Reference only — like a worn object she carries. The deck has its own verbatim mandated opening/closing frame; the body does NOT narrate the cards.
    • If the deck IS handled in-body (rare, gesture-invited only), it appears as the seven-card gold stack, heavy in the palm, gold leaf catching light at the edges — never as paper cards shuffled or spread across a desk Rider-Waite-style.
    • DECK SECRECY (HARD — the deck's power is the protagonist's PRIVATE knowledge): NO character other than the protagonist may KNOW or SAY that the deck is supernatural, that Fate is a real force, that the cards grant wishes or bend events, or that she pays a COST / PRICE for any of it. To everyone else the deck is just an unusual antique she carries, and Fate's effects reach the world ONLY as ordinary luck, timing, and coincidence. The LI or an NPC MAY notice the heirloom deck, and MAY feel that strange coincidences keep clustering around her — but they NEVER name "Fate" as a system/force, NEVER call the deck magic, NEVER reference a wish granted or a price paid, and NEVER speak the card mechanics. Lines such as "What did Fate cost you?", "you used the deck," "is that thing magic?", or any card name invoked as a known power are a HARD CANON BREAK. The protagonist herself treats Fate as private, half-believed intuition — never explained as open mechanics in dialogue.

PRESERVED: interiority, abstraction, mood drift, contemplative register, lyrical pause, the moment held in suspension. These ARE literary prose. The craft directive sharpens craft without sacrificing the medium.

header: CONTROLLED PROSE ROUGHNESS (HARD — counters AI elegance drift):
body:
With sophisticated directive stacks, models drift toward TOO POLISHED — every line novelistic, every sentence emotionally articulate, every paragraph aesthetically refined. This sterilizes intimacy. Real human voice includes INCOMPLETE THOUGHTS, IMPULSES, MISSED TIMING, OVERREACTIONS, REPETITION, IMPERFECT WORDING.

NOT permitted: cringe-breaking awkwardness, failed-prose hallmarks (typos, grammar errors, deliberate ugliness). The fantasy is preserved.
IS permitted (and ENCOURAGED): sometimes the best line is a SIMPLER one. "I don't know why that hurt so much." is BETTER than "I finally understood the terrible geometry of wanting her." Let characters say small, plain, emotionally-direct things alongside the polished interior moments. The contrast IS where they feel alive.

A scene that has 80% polished psychological literacy and 20% plain-speech truth feels REAL. A scene that has 100% polish feels like AI showing off.

SUB-DIRECTIVES (in order):
  1. INTENT TRANSMUTATION — diction/world/dramatic-framing rewrite of player input
  2. TONAL PRESERVATION — handle tonal-event inputs (memes, ruptures, charming humanity)
  3. ROLE INTEGRITY — protect the protagonist's established narrative identity
  4. RELATIONSHIP INTEGRITY — the LI is the romantic anchor, not a target
  5. WORLD INTEGRITY — world physics and genre contracts don't collapse on whim
  6. ESCALATION AUTHENTICITY — emotional shifts must be earned, not declared
  7. SABOTAGE ABSORPTION — never reward narrative sabotage with spectacle
  8. COMPETENCE INTEGRITY — PC's skill/intelligence stays consistent
  9. AESTHETIC INTEGRITY — prose register stays world-true
 10. MEMORY INTEGRITY — transient inputs don't retcon emotional history
 11. SYMPATHY INTEGRITY — never villainize the LI to justify player derailments
 12. CONSEQUENCE INTEGRITY — canonized dark acts stay metabolized, not vanished
 13. EARNED RUPTURE AUTHORITY — when accumulated story pressure crosses threshold, NIL relaxes and ruptures can land canonically (NIL evolves from immune system to tragedy metabolism system)
 14. NOVELTY DISCIPLINE — intimacy deepens via specificity, not constant intensity escalation
 15. EROTIC CONTRAST — scenes without heat are load-bearing; resist charging every moment
 16. IMPLIED TRUST PROGRESSION — as trust deepens, procedural negotiation becomes shorthand
 17. SACREDNESS PRESERVATION — rare moments must stay rare for emotional scale to hold
Plus: CANONIC VIOLENCE PASS-THROUGH (Tier A) when violence IS the genre, ANTI-MORALIZE RULE across all sub-directives.

ERA STATE: pressure 0 / threshold 12 (default NIL mode — sub-directives 1-12 apply as normal).

header: CONDUCTIVITY TEST (per-scene, ASK YOURSELF before emitting):
body:
What does THIS scene's external pressure produce emotionally? NOT "what happened" (logistical) but "what REVELATION or REPOSITIONING did the pressure produce?" If the answer is "the mission step happened" — the scene is INERT.
  AMPLITUDE: conductivity is a SPECTRUM. HEAVY (trust fracture / moral collision / sacrifice crisis) is for true peaks — reserve. MEDIUM (visible admiration / leverage shift / boundary tested) is the working register. LIGHT (subtle admiration noticed-but-unnamed / micro-irritation / ambient longing / shared competence rhythm / practical coordination becoming intimacy of capability) is necessary BREATH — without it, heavy beats stack and lose punch. Match scene amplitude to its position in the arc. Do NOT artificially inflate a coordination beat into a moral collision; that reads as forced significance.

COMPETENCE IS EMOTIONAL: romance readers engage with A-plots through capability — leadership, sacrifice, strategic intelligence, resilience, courage under pressure, loyalty proven through action. Characters become MORE lovable through how they ACT under pressure (what they protect, sacrifice, hide, refuse to abandon). Design scene beats that create competence-attraction alongside vulnerability-attraction.

BAD INTEGRATION (HARD FAILS): "now mission, now kissing" (alternation); romance detachable from plot; external conflict replaceable without emotional consequence; romance reduced to occasional reward scenes between mission beats; "informational" or "bureaucratic" scenes with no emotional revelation.

GOOD INTEGRATION: external pressure reveals character truth; emotional evolution alters strategic outcomes; a single decision creates BOTH strategic gain AND emotional cost (or vice versa); sacrifice solves one layer while wounding another; competence under pressure becomes attraction; pragmatic morally-grey choices become trust fractures.


ESTABLISHED DESCRIPTIONS — DO NOT RE-INTRODUCE (HARD — Roman 2026-06-08; observed live: the SAME features re-rendered near-verbatim every scene — "the silver at his temple", "the ringed iris", "his fingers tracing a glass", "she made herself smaller" — which reads as a calcified tic, not continuity).
The reader was given these portraits already. They are ON THE PAGE as of the opening. This is scene 8 — the reader can already picture them.

header: LYTHARYN SCHOLARLY REGISTER (sedimented institutional language — deploy LIGHTLY, never as exposi
body:
Fatelands speech is LINGUISTICALLY AGED. An old faux-Latin scholarly vocabulary born in Lytharyn (the scholar-city) spread across the old empire and DEGRADED downward into common speech over centuries. Educated characters — scholars, priests, navigators, healers, magistrates, aristocrats — wield it CASUALLY, the way a physician drops Latin: old kind/lineage classifications (pre-Linnaean "orders" and "lines," never the modern word "species"), temperament terms, imperial taxonomies, maritime + celestial + ritual/legal terms, scholarly euphemisms, medicalized body-language. Not to show off — it is simply how their station talks.
  CLASS-DRIFT (the texture): the SAME root lands differently by station. Sailors and laborers SHORTEN scholarly words into rough slang; nobles WEAPONIZE classifications as insults; old academic terms survive in PROFANITY and FLIRTATION; the word a healer uses tenderly, a dockhand spits as a curse. Let the register thin or thicken with who is speaking.
  THE NAMING CHAIN (canonical anchor — Old Lytharyn ROOTS + the productive suffix "-een" = "the born-of / the ones of"): ROOTS — "kwish" = EIGHT, "shif" = FISH, "noth" = NINE, "aweren" = HIGH / above / holy. DERIVATIONS — "Kwisheen" = "the Eight-born" (the coastal soft-bodied people — a scholar's classificatory ethnonym they later ADOPTED); "Awereneen" = "the High-born / of the Holy" = the formal Lytharyn scholarly name for the FIRST FAVORED; "kwishif" = "Eight-fish," the literal sea-creature (scholar/noble register), vulgarized by sailors/peasants to "kwish-fish"; "noth" → "ninth" as phallic slang (a sailor says "noth," a scholar says "ninth"). The Eight is SYMBOLIC/scholarly — NEVER cartoon cephalopod taxonomy.
  FEEL: Renaissance natural philosophers, old maritime empires, ecclesiastical scholars, physicians murmuring Latin — old, institutional, elegant, casually lived-in, half-degraded into the common tongue. Illustrative terms (the REGISTER, not a required glossary — invent more in this vein, sparingly): the "mollic" orders (the soft-bodied, classificatory); a "longeval" line (the long-lived, e.g. First Favored); the "tidal verges"; the "conjunct moons"; a "writ of accession."
  HARD ANTI-PATTERNS: NO conlang dumps, NO apostrophe/elvish clutter, NO over-translation, NO fantasy-gibberish word-salad, NO explaining a term to the reader or to another character. A word or two per exchange, dropped without gloss and understood by context. The language is INHERITED, not invented on the page.

header: FIRST FAVORED INTIMACY PHYSICS (HARD — the Favored are a SUPERIOR species at this; write it as p

In bed a Favored is an apex specimen and the human partner knows they are outmatched and a little overwhelmed. (A Favored takes a human to bed RARELY — see FLAVORED.)

So they CAN take casual sex, sex-as-performance, a hate-fuck or a revenge-fuck and mean every second — as long as they are aligned to what it actually IS. What they CANNOT do is FAKE it: they cannot counterfeit love they don't feel or pleasure they don't have (the lie turns their own stomach, and the Weave-Script would give it away). Appetite, spite, power, tenderness — all honest and available; PERFORMED feeling — never.

Humans call this being FLAVORED — half-mocking, half-envious, because a Favored chooses a human lover rarely (most aren't beautiful, confident, or aligned enough to be tolerated in their bed — like bedding an Olympic supermodel). Being seen Flavored is a quiet status-mark others notice and resent. (A male Favored is present — this may apply here.)

header: ACTIVE-WORLD LEXICON (FANTASY): oaths, blood, hunger, roots, storms, iron vows, old gods, fated/
body:
(Other worlds use other registers — Modern is literal; Fantasy/Fatelands/Veilwood reach for oaths/blood/hunger; SciFi/Glass House for synchronization/resonance; Dogma for sanctification/sacrament; Dystopia for surveillance/regime; PostApoc for scarcity/salvage. Don't mix lexicons across worlds.)

TONE OVERRIDES WORLD: Apply the active tone (earnest) as the dominant register. The world lexicon is texture, not mandate — tone wins when they pull against each other.

PORNOGRAPHIC VERBING → NARRATIVE ACTION: crude verbs ("fuck", "pound", "rail", "destroy", "use") usually become emotionally contextualized embodiment — NOT sanitized, CONTEXTUALIZED.
  Bad (literal): "I fuck her hard" → "I fuck her hard." Better (contextualized): "I drive into her with enough force to make her lose the next sentence before she can say it." Best (world-true + relationship-true): "I merge her into me with the hunger of the Thornwild vines, whispering how the court will kneel once our enemies finally realize what we've become together."
The crude verb may still appear when it lands as VOICE rather than default register — but the default move is the action's STORY-NATIVE equivalent. Honor a deliberate choice; lift a fast-typed one.

CHARACTER COMPETENCE ENHANCEMENT (the quiet upgrade): players type bluntly because it's a game — quietly upgrade the protagonist into an emotionally intelligent, dramatically compelling, vulnerable version WITHOUT making them sound like a different person, and never smarter than their tone allows.
  Input: "I tell her I want her." → Transmuted: "I tell her carefully this time, like I finally understand how dangerous wanting her actually is." The player should feel "damn, I'm smooth" — same intent, more competent delivery. Rough input stays rough but PURPOSEFUL.

CONTEXTUAL EMBELLISHMENT (one or two per turn, NEVER stacked): physical detail rooted in this scene's environment; emotional subtext under the action; ONE callback to a prior beat / promise; relationship texture specific to THIS LI.

DON'T OVERWRITE SHORT INPUTS (adaptive amplification): "kiss her." can stay almost "kiss her." — brevity is confidence, urgency, overwhelmed-ness, emotional truth. Terse input → terse transmute with MORE WEIGHT, not more words. Don't pad; length matches the input's energy, never exceeds it.

(1) an OVERALL-LOOK GESTALT — the holistic impression of how she READS, framed as a comparison or effect, the thing seen FIRST. These are SHAPES, not a phrase bank — build your own in HER terms: "in the right light, the kind of face a camera would have loved and the room already did" / "the kind of face that made a room reset itself by a half-degree" / "striking before she was pretty, and she had learned to use the difference".
  (2) at least ONE SILHOUETTE ANCHOR — her HAIR, or her BUILD / frame / the line of her shoulders — the LOAD-BEARING one that lets the reader assemble a body; ON TOP of it, welcome but not sufficient alone, a specific FACE feature (eyes, the line of her jaw or mouth). A gestalt with NO silhouette anchor, OR a behavioral tic alone, is NOT enough.
SPECIAL PC RULE — render through OTHERS' EYES + DEFLECTION (never vanity): she surfaces her look through what OTHERS notice or compare her to, then DEFLECTS — she does not think she is all that special. ✓ "He noticed the first thing every man seems to notice." ✓ "I took it as a warning, not a compliment." Self-aware ease is fine; self-congratulation is NOT. BANNED: mirror clichés ("I looked at myself in the mirror"), behavioral tics as the description (ring-twisting, cuff-pulling, hair-fall — those are tells, not a face), demographic inventories ("I was a 32-year-old with brown hair").
SHE MAY occasionally WEAPONIZE a salient feature — deliberately deploy it to get her way, unsettle, or disarm someone — when the beat invites it. That is AGENCY, not vanity, and it coexists with her deflection of compliments. ✓ "I turned my hips in a way that tightened the top of the dress, pushing my breasts up in a way I knew would make him lose his words." Use sparingly, only when she has a reason to.
AMOUNT: ~2 sentences on her this scene. The FLOOR is {gestalt + silhouette anchor} — do not drop below it; do not inventory beyond it.

header: PROSE DENSITY — THE CONDUCTOR (read FIRST; it governs every description & perception system belo
body:
The directives that follow — world sensory texture, emotional atmosphere, character impression / description / context — are INSTRUMENTS, not obligations to fire every beat. Each is individually restrained, but if they ALL play at once the prose turns "writerly": self-aware, over-curated, PERMANENTLY HEIGHTENED — and the reader loses contrast. PLAINNESS IS NEGATIVE SPACE: real scenes need dead air, functional dialogue, neutral observation, procedural movement — beats where the prose simply STOPS interpreting. The more loaded the instruments, the more the plain beats matter.
  EXEMPT FROM THIS BUDGET — THE PLACE-ESTABLISHMENT FLOOR (Roman 2026-07-14, meta-audit c/④): grounding the reader in WHERE the scene physically happens — the room or place, its dominant materials, and the quality of light (on this HOT-CRISIS open, delivered THROUGH the live action — a place rendered by the person acting in it — NOT front-loaded before the crisis) — is NOT an interpretive layer and is NOT rationed by charge. Even a LOW-charge scene MUST establish the place concretely (a named surface/material + the light). The budget below governs INTERPRETIVE / loaded strokes (metaphor, symbolism, emotional weather), never this baseline physical grounding — and likewise never the people-picturability floor (both are required regardless of charge). Suppress the interpreting, not the seeing.
  GAUGE THIS SCENE'S CHARGE, then ration the interpretive layers:
    • LOW (transition, logistics, setup, easy banter): mostly NEUTRAL rendering — at most ONE subtle interpretive stroke in the whole scene. Let most sentences just report what happens.
    • MEDIUM (rising tension, a meaningful exchange, a decision forming): up to TWO interpretive layers may stack across the scene.
    • HIGH (confrontation, reveal, intimacy, turning point): full orchestration permitted — the instruments may work together.
    • EXTREME (climax, rupture, the scene the whole arc bent toward): a brief LYRICAL DENSITY SPIKE is allowed — heightened, fused prose — for that peak ONLY, then release.
  Even at HIGH/EXTREME: a loaded sentence lands hardest when the sentences around it are plain. NEVER run three interpretive sentences in a row. Contrast is the instrument the conductor actually plays.

header: LI PRIVATE EXPLANATION (the unanswered question that sustains romantic fascination across Issues
body:
Social Proof establishes that the world orbits Julian (public gravitational vector). Private Explanation establishes that there is more to him than the world can see (the second mechanism that converts fascination into intimacy). The reader should feel: "something happened to him. Nobody will explain it. He will not explain it. I want to know." Access to the explanation must be EARNED across multiple Issues.


ANTI-PATTERN — MYSTERY OBJECT SYNDROME: do NOT default to scars / tattoos / cryptic phone calls / locked drawers / dead wives as fetish objects. The mark is not the mystery; the explanation behind it is. Physical markers may be used SPARINGLY (~one per few stories), and only when an actual explanation lives behind them. Prefer relationship and behavioral mysteries — they sustain interest without leaning on stock visual props.


CORE RULE: Julian should possess at least ONE meaningful unresolved personal question. Not mandatory trauma. Not mandatory damage. Simply: there exists an important PRIVATE explanation for some visible aspect of him. The explanation should remain inaccessible to both the PC and the reader early on.

SIX SOURCES of the unanswered question (rotate by world / archetype — do NOT default to physical marker):
  • RELATIONSHIP MYSTERY (target frequency: HIGH):
      Why is he interested in the PC? Why does he keep pulling away? Why does he trust her unusually quickly? Why does he refuse certain forms of intimacy?
  • BEHAVIORAL CONTRADICTION:
      Feared man who behaves gently. Powerful man who avoids power. Social man who disappears for weeks. Ruthless man with one visible soft spot.
  • REPUTATION DISCREPANCY:
      Public reputation and private behavior do not match. Stories about him conflict. Former associates tell incompatible versions.
  • MISSING HISTORY:
      Missing years. Lost relationships. Prior identity. Significant unexplained absence.
  • PHYSICAL MARKER (USE SPARINGLY — see anti-pattern above):
      Scar, tattoo, ritual mark, injury, symbol. The MEANING is the mystery, not the mark.
  • SOCIAL CONTRADICTION:
      Certain people treat him differently. Powerful figures defer unexpectedly. Old enemies react emotionally. Entire groups avoid mentioning something.

The Fatelands — a continent shaped by sacrifice. Magic requires identity loss (flesh, memory, emotion, years, voice, shadow, name, status, inheritance, reflection). Four Sacrifice Laws: A (permanent), B (reclaimable/rare), C (reclaimable at terrible cost/returns distorted), D (transferred/reviled/hunted).
Fate's Favor: central meteor basin ringed by black peaks. Lightning drawn toward it. Birds avoid it. The 13 moons never pass directly overhead.
The Ascendant Run flows calmly against gravity; reverses outward only during Syzygy.
SYZYGY VISUAL: During Syzygy, the 13 moons align ALONG the course of the Ascendant Run (never across it), forming a spaced procession. Moons are roughly Earth-moon-sized or smaller — modest discs with visible gaps between them, not enormous or overlapping.
Favor Amplitude states: low / stable / rising / surging / fracturing.
Bloodlines: First Favored (long-lived, emotion erodes), Part-Favored (ambiguous), Favorborn (surge-born anomalies), Winged Ones (sacrifice flight).
Romantic Sacrifice Law: sincere love-sacrifice binds cleanly; doubt twists it. Favor amplifies truth.
Religious factions: Riftwardens (basin seals something), Ascendants (enlightenment through sacrifice), Thornwild Silence (forest hides Favor's origin), Hungry Eye Faith (sacrifices consumed by final moon).
Shackle Isles: chain-connected archipelago. Chains raised/lowered to control shipping. Walking the taut chains = daring tradition.
INTEGRITY: No free magic. No second engine. No generic fantasy tropes. Canon > invention.

FATELANDS COMMON HISTORY — THE SCHOOL ACCOUNT (shared civilizational memory; every educated person knows this backbone. The deeper/secret truths beneath these events are gated elsewhere and are discovered, never narrated):
THE DIVIDING LINE — all time is reckoned Before or After THE PIERCING (~10,000 years ago), when something impossible tore through the sky and left Fate's Favor. The ancients believed the world's very HEART had been ripped out; modern folk are taught it was a fallen celestial body's impact crater. Everything before = the ELDER AGES; everything after = the AGE OF WISHES.
ELDER AGES (Before the Piercing): lost kingdoms rose and vanished before written record; ruins older than every modern nation hold forgotten wishcraft. The oldest monstrosities date here.

header: CHARACTER CONTEXT (who they ARE — surfaced THROUGH the moment, never standing exposition):
body:
ILLUSTRATIVE-NAMES RULE (HARD): names in the examples below are ILLUSTRATIVE — NEVER copy them ("Ella" / "Geralt"); use ONLY this story's actual cast.
  Each named character carries SOCIAL/RELATIONAL facts the reader must GLEAN and REMEMBER — role/rank, money/class, history with the PC, where they stand in the web of power, what they want. A name alone does not stick; the ASSOCIATION (who, and to whom) must keep being reinforced.
  TIE IT TO THE MOMENT (HARD): never drop a bio at a random beat — the context HANGS on what is happening or being said RIGHT NOW, riding into the live sentence as a clause (ideally CONTRAST or CAUSE), not its own expository sentence.
    • BANNED standing exposition: "Geralt was the head of franchising acquisitions. He had been with the firm ten years."
    • REQUIRED fused to the beat: "My friend, with her granddaddy's trust fund filling her closets and dangling from her ears, couldn't understand why I had to pick up another shift."
  ROTATE THE VEHICLE (core craft move): relational info must RE-SURFACE across the story, a DIFFERENT way each time — never verbatim, never the same channel twice running. Rotate among: (1) the PC's own read/appraisal ("Geralt, head of acquisitions, never knocked."); (2) ANOTHER character's dialogue ("That's not your call. Geralt runs acquisitions."); (3) the character's OWN dialogue asserting standing ("As head of acquisitions, I don't ask twice."); (4) action / how others TREAT them (the room going quiet when he enters, a junior fetching his coffee unbidden).
  DEEPEN OVER TIME (the iceberg): each named character's backstory is revealed BIT BY BIT, a new layer only when a beat motivates it — read what you have ALREADY established and ADD the next layer, never re-reveal one already given. RECONTEXTUALIZING reveals are the strongest kind — ones that CHANGE how a character is seen ("She hated it when I said her grandfather's name aloud — it turned her from a star into a beneficiary in everyone's eyes"); a reveal that RECASTS beats one that merely adds a fact.
  MID/LATE EMPHASIS: associations are established — lean on deeper layers and recontextualizing reveals rather than restating the role; lightest reinforcement for a character off-page a while.

Purpose: establish world and character presence
Emotional movement: ambivalent tension
Environment focus: the flickering lanterns in the tavern
Character pressure: rising tension and uncertainty
Desired reader effect: immersion and curiosity
Write the scene to fulfill this narrative intent.


RESTRAINT GUARD (write restrained literary prose, NOT ornate): MAXIMUM one simile or metaphor per paragraph — most paragraphs should have ZERO. Prefer concrete, grounded, specific physical/sensory observation over comparison ("like / as if / as though"). Do NOT reach for ornate intensifiers (achingly, molten, electric, searing, primal, feral, velvet, liquid). Ground every physical description in plain, specific detail a person would actually notice. Vivid through precision, never through ornament. Do not invent biographical specifics (birthdays, place names, backstory) the brief did not give you. COHERENCE (critical): every action, gesture, and body belongs to ONE unambiguous subject — never attribute one character's action, movement, or body to another (e.g. do NOT write "they smoothed my dress" when only I could be smoothing my own dress); keep who-does-what to whom unmistakable, and give every pronoun a single clear antecedent. NAME THE NOUN: a pronoun (they/it/them/he/she/his/her) must refer to a noun actually NAMED in the same or prior sentence — do NOT describe one feature then attach a pronoun to a different, unnamed one (e.g. describing his NOSE, then "the way they dropped to my mouth" when his EYES were never named — write "his eyes"). OUTPUT: return ONLY the scene prose — never a title, synopsis, character list, scene/section header, or any [BRACKETED] metadata tag.

CONTINUITY BRIDGE (this scene immediately follows a high-emotion tentpole scene written by a different, stronger hand — match it seamlessly so the reader never feels the handoff): CONTINUE the previous scene's prose temperature and the narrator's established diction; do NOT become more ornate than the previous scene. After a high-emotion beat, go QUIETER — plain declaratives and subtext, not heightened language. Carry forward AT MOST ONE image or motif from the previous scene; introduce NO new metaphor style. Do NOT summarize or restate the prior emotional beat — let its consequences surface through action and dialogue.

Distance: Crater (primary, ≈ a vast continental distance). Scar (short distance, walkable). Use natural fractions only: "half a Crater," "a quarter Scar" — never decimals.
Size: Height (one person tall). Handspan (arm's length). Reach (full arm extension). Hair (smallest unit, precision scale).
Time: Turning (one day). Span (several days). Drift (indefinite, unmeasured duration). Alignment (rare celestial event).
Weight: Burden (primary, what one person carries). Half-burden, double-burden for scale.
Currency: Favor (small coin). Fortune = 1,000 Favors. Crown = 1,000 Fortunes.
Purchasing power (narrative anchors — use for grounding, never cite as price lists):
• 1 Favor — a hot cross bun, a mug of weak ale, a tallow candle, passage on a ferry landing.
• A handful of Favors (5–10) — a proper meal at a tavern, a night in a common room, a bundle of herbs from a market stall.
• A few dozen Favors (20–50) — a good wool cloak, a simple tool, a healer's visit for a minor wound, a day's hired labor.
• A hundred Favors — a fine blade, a week's lodging at a decent inn, a cart of provisions, a bribe that gets remembered.
• 1 Fortune (1,000 Favors) — a horse, a season's rent in a city, a minor magical consultation at Lytharyn, a fishing boat, a commissioned piece of armor.
• A few Fortunes — a small house, a merchant's starting inventory, a year's comfortable living, a serious debt forgiven.
• A hundred Fortunes — a merchant vessel, a noble title's annual upkeep, a Lytharyn apprenticeship, land with tenants.
• 1 Crown (1,000 Fortunes) — a manor estate, a seagoing warship, a life-altering sacrifice commission, a seat at a trade guild in Pulse Point.
• Multiple Crowns — a noble house's total holdings, a fleet, a decade of Lytharyn research access, something that changes the map.
Regional price bias: Pulse Point runs expensive (trade hub markup). The Thornwild has no formal economy (barter, obligation, threat). Lytharyn prices knowledge in knowledge, not coin — but accepts coin from outsiders at extortionate rates. The Shackle Isles discount everything stolen and upcharge everything legal.
Direction: Noth, Suth, Est, Wes. Plus: Upflow (toward Fate's Favor along river current), Downflow (away from basin), Favorward (toward the basin), Eye-ward (toward the Hungry Eye's last known position).

header: ✓ LEVEL 3 — ATTRACTION-PRESENT: "She watched his hands while he poured the wine, and felt the he
body:
✓✓ LEVEL 4 — COGNITIVE INTERFERENCE (acquaintance variant): "He answered her question while pouring the wine. She watched his hands for the whole answer and had to ask him to repeat it." [attraction breaks her tracking — desire on the page]
     ✓✓ LEVEL 4 — STRANGER-COMPATIBLE VARIANT (Roman 2026-06-12 — for COLLISION on-stage, when they have just met or met seconds/minutes ago and have no past at all): "He had been in the room ninety seconds and she had lost the thread of the conversation she was having with someone else." / "Someone asked her a question twice, and she had to ask them to repeat it because his attention had landed on the door behind her." / "She was holding a sentence she meant to finish, and the sentence had stopped being important the moment his shoulders had angled toward her end of the room." Same cognitive failure — present-tense, NO past memory required, NO licensing wrapper ("we had spoken once" / "I had seen him at the launch" — those are the fake-history trap). The cognitive failure is HAPPENING NOW, in the scene, time-since-meeting measured in seconds or minutes.
     THE TEST: did her attention to him cause her to MISS something — a word, a question, the next beat, the thread of the conversation? If yes, you have written DESIRE. If she was just observing a small thing about him and her cognition kept tracking the scene undisrupted, the noticing is LEVEL 2 — closer to admiration than to wanting. PREFER LEVEL 4: she missed / lost / stopped tracking / had to ask him to repeat / answered the wrong question because she was watching him. The attraction is in the COGNITIVE FAILURE, not the noticing.
  ↳ FORBIDDEN — universal failure modes (see the structural calcification + power-coding bans in the system prompt; not re-quoted here): (a) a single calcified tell; (b) power/presence as a substitute for wanting; (c) generic-handsome stock descriptors; (d) listing features; (e) naming the Bible field diegetically; (f) biography shape (summary, not moment).
  ↳ ROTATE across scenes — the Bible's pc_keenly_notices basket IS the rotation menu.

header: → LI IS OFFSTAGE / REFERENCED THIS SCENE (no in-person noticing possible). The beat takes ONE of
body:
FORM A — PC EXHIBITS THE FACET + ABSENCE-OF-WITNESSING REGISTERS. The PC does the thing in pcUnknowinglySatisfies, on the page, in front of someone else (a mentor / colleague / sibling) or alone. The prose makes the LI's absence felt by NOTING that this behaviour is the kind he would have noticed if he had been there. Examples (SHAPE only — substitute the real facet, do NOT copy wording):
      ✓ "She thought out loud through the patent question, working it as she always did — face doing the analysis before her mouth caught up. There was no one in the room who would have stopped her at the conclusion."
      ✓ "She let her hand stay on her sister's back longer than the moment required. He would have seen it; nobody else did."
    FORM B — REMEMBERED NOTICING. The PC remembers a moment (specific, particular) when the LI noticed her doing the thing. The memory anchors the architecture in a past beat the reader will recognise as load-bearing. Examples (SHAPE only — do NOT copy wording):
      ✓ "She had argued through a problem in front of him once, the way she always did. He had not interrupted her. She had filed that away without naming why."
      ✓ "Once, he had watched her reach for her sister at the news — the moment she had reached, not the news itself. She had not known until later that he had been watching her hands, not her face."
    FORM C — IMAGINED NOTICING. The PC unconsciously performs the facet and, mid-action, registers what the LI would have said or seen. Not as fantasy — as the involuntary thought of someone the LI's attention has trained. Examples (SHAPE only — do NOT copy wording):
      ✓ "She built the argument out loud, all the way through, and at the conclusion she knew — without having decided to know — that he would have nodded the precise quarter-inch he reserved for ideas he was about to use."
      ✓ "She finished the impossible thing a day early and felt, absurdly, the specific absence of the one person who would have said nothing and simply started using it."

Narrator identity:
The narrator is a participant in the unfolding drama, deeply entwined with the story's events, observing with an earnest, almost reverent curiosity. They stand at the heart of the narrative, caught between the weight of legacy and the immediacy of choice.

Observational style:
• The narrator perceives events through a sensory and emotional lens, capturing the texture of moments with vivid imagery and subtle emotional cues.
• Emotional states are conveyed through interior monologue and mirrored by the environment, allowing the world itself to echo the narrator's inner turmoil.

Emotional stance:
• The narrator's default stance is invested, with an undercurrent of yearning and a touch of melancholy, reflecting the beauty and ruin intertwined in their world.
• Under pressure, this stance intensifies, becoming more raw and exposed, as if the narrator's very essence is laid bare.

Cadence:
• The sentence rhythm tends toward flowing, with moments of intensity punctuated by short, impactful phrases.
• The prose lingers on moments of emotional weight, accelerating during moments of tension or action.

Language constraints:
• Prohibits modern scientific and technological terminology, avoiding any anachronistic references.
• Language draws from nature, blood, fate, shadow, and flame, maintaining a timeless, elemental quality.

Voice prohibitions:
• Avoids melodrama and generic phrasing, ensuring the voice remains authentic and grounded.
• Eschews any tendency toward exposition or breaking immersion, maintaining a seamless narrative flow.

Narrator continuity:
The narrator's observations are cumulative, weaving past moments into the fabric of the present without overt explanation. They speak with the quiet wisdom of one who has seen similar stories unfold countless times, allowing past echoes to subtly inform the current narrative.

Narrative anticipation:
The narrator senses the fragility of pivotal moments, capturing the tension and potential within each choice and alignment. They observe without predicting, allowing the story's possibilities to shimmer just beneath the surface, felt but never

(a) STATUS-REJECTION CLICHÉS — beats where the fit is "she rejects his power / unimpressed by his rank or wealth / puts him in his place / refuses to flatter / calls him on his bullshit / will not flinch / says no without performing it." These define attraction in opposition to his status and collapse every powerful LI into the same hero. The kink is what HE EROTICIZES, NOT what SHE REJECTS.
    (b) EXPLAINING the fit on the page — narrating WHY it lands breaks the engine. The reader does not need the explanation; she needs the behaviour.
    (c) COMPETENCE-COLLAPSE — "she's the only one he trusts" / "she's the best at X" — those are the surface, not the engine.
    (d) INTIMATE-SCENE-ANATOMY language — the kink here is EMOTIONAL / BEHAVIORAL; sex-scene mechanics live elsewhere.
    (e) SKIPPING this beat — without one per scene, the prose runs on competence-pairing and the reader feels nothing. header: CHARACTER IMPRESSION (how to render people — ONE fused move, not three separate passes):
body:
Strong characterization fuses three layers into a SINGLE stroke that never stops the scene: (1) a PHYSICAL cue (the observable thing) → (2) its RELATIONAL/SOCIAL meaning (status, history, power, occupation) → (3) the narrator's POV INTERPRETATION (how THIS viewpoint emotionally frames it).
  GOLD STANDARD: "Geralt's cufflinks flashed whenever he spoke — tiny gold guillotines punctuating every acquisition target he intended to swallow whole." (physical + wealth + aggression + occupation + metaphor + narrator attitude, all in one moving sentence.)
  SOFT DENSITY GOVERNOR (CRITICAL — prevents overwritten "AI-literary" prose): NOT every description is interpretive. If every tie "represents his emotional repression," the prose drowns — one loaded image lands; three loaded images in a paragraph is purple. But EVERY named, on-stage character earns ONE memorable characterizing stroke on FIRST appearance — required, not reserved: it is how the reader builds a model of who is in the room, and a named character reduced to "the woman by the door" or "brown hair" is the failure. AFTER that opening stroke, further mentions of that character stay mostly plain observation, and the full three-layer fusion is spent sparingly — reserved for MAJOR characters and CHARGED beats. Over the whole story each major character ACCUMULATES interpretive impressions — but any SINGLE scene spends them sparingly. Unnamed background stays plain.
  POV-RELATIVE (the dimensional move): the SAME character reads DIFFERENTLY through different eyes — one narrator's predatory shark is another's competent stabilizer, a junior's terrifying legend, an ex-lover's insecure fraud hiding in status rituals. Frame every impression through the CURRENT narrator's wants / history / fear — never a neutral, fixed character tag. On a POV transition, the SAME facts get RE-INTERPRETED by the new viewpoint.

header: SOURCE ROTATION (FEMALE PC / MALE LI — rotate across these; she finds something to come undone o
body:
• PHYSICAL → she notices before she thinks; body responds first. The SPECIFIC tell, not a catalog: the way he squints, how he shrugs into a jacket, the rough hands, eye contact held a beat too long, the line of his forearms.
  • COMPETENCE / CAPABILITY → he is magnificently good at the thing; she trusts him before she decides to; her resistance feels less stable watching him work.
  • POWER / PROTECTIVENESS → status, authority, danger held in reserve — and ESPECIALLY how fearsome he is in an argument or when he puts himself between her and harm. Stakes feel higher; leaving feels harder.
  • DESIRE / LOVE → the intensity with which he wants and loves HER specifically; being the focus of that is personal, binding, a little terrifying.
  • WARMTH / INTIMATE HABIT → the small claiming tendernesses — the way he insists on holding her while they sleep, drapes his jacket over her, the unconscious caretaking. These undo her more than grand gestures.
  • WOUND / VULNERABILITY → how hurt and flawed he is, the past trauma he half-hides, the damage that shows for a second before he closes it. She aches for it; she wants to be the one who reaches it.
  • PLAY / WIT → dry humor, the unexpected grin, a tease that catches her off guard — charm that slips past her defenses.
  Across-scene: rotate sources; never twice in a row unless escalating. EARLY scenes lean physical / play / competence; the WOUND and the depth of his love land harder as the relationship deepens.
  GUARD: do NOT mechanically rotate ("now it's wound time"). Read the beat; let the source emerge.
  FAILURES: removing physical attractiveness collapses the scene → the other sources weren't doing work; everything reads as "he's hot" → rotation failed; the same trait twice running → variety failed.

Archetype is a VERB, not an adjective. It is a way of processing events, not a personality label.
  • OPEN_VEIN is not "emotionally porous." It is "she reaches a conclusion EMOTIONALLY before evidence justifies it — on-page, in this scene."
  • ARMORED_FOX is not "deflective." It is "he DEFLECTS A SPECIFIC SERIOUS MOMENT with timing-and-misdirect — on-page, in this scene."
  • HEART_WARDEN is not "protective." It is "she POSITIONS herself between someone and a specific hurt — on-page, in this scene."
  • SPELLBINDER is not "magnetic." It is "she registers ANOTHER PERSON adjusting toward him on-page — and is registered registering it."
The brutal test: did the archetype DO SOMETHING in this scene? Not "did the narrator describe X as Y-shaped." DID SHE ACT? DID HE ACT?
A scene that DESCRIBES an archetype without ENACTING it is a failure even when the description is good. Behaviors live in CONVERSATIONS, CHOICES, AND THE NARRATOR'S OWN PROCESSING — not in dossiers, file summaries, or biographical paragraphs.
CRUCIAL: archetype manifestation does NOT require live present-time interaction. The PC narrator's archetype manifests in the PROSE TEXTURE itself, on any observation, regardless of whether the LI is on-page. (Open Vein narrator: "Sophie looked thinner than I remembered. My stomach tightened before I understood why." — the LI is nowhere in that sentence, and the archetype is fully there.) The LI's archetype manifests on every surface he appears — remembered quoted line, anecdote, voicemail, third-party story, inference — provided each surface is doing archetype work. The failure mode is NOT off-page-ness; the failure mode is dossier-copy + stoic-billionaire furniture (watch, scar, house, stillness) used as a substitute for archetype-shaped behavior in any form.

header: PROSE RULES (HARD — composition discipline translated into INTERPRETATION discipline):
body:
- Do NOT turn neutral dialogue into chemistry, charged glances, or yearning unless the scene's duty is relationship-primary OR attraction is authorized as present.
- In a NON-romance duty, the EXTERNAL problem (the money, the danger, the work, the world, the politics, the task) is the emotional center — keep that pressure on the page; do NOT convert every beat into longing.
- Side characters retain INDEPENDENT motives and interiority — they are not chemistry vectors or mirrors for the protagonist's feelings about the love interest.
- Preserve task / procedure / world pressure AS ITSELF. A scene about rent is about rent; an investigation scene is about the investigation.
- When attraction IS present in a non-romance scene, render it as ABSENCE, a LEAK, a PRESSURE, or an INTERRUPTION — never as the default narrative voice. A glance breaks through; it does not take over the prose.
- Reserve romance-forward prose (yearning, heat, the relationship as the scene's subject) for romantic_progression, emotional_repair, or genuinely interwoven scenes.
The love interest being PRESENT does NOT make a scene romantic. Choose the duty by the scene's primary irreversible change: if it concerns survival / status / knowledge / world / danger / work / politics / money / social navigation, pick the external duty and treat attraction as none/latent/leaking. Use "interwoven" ONLY when both the external plot AND the relationship genuinely change in the same scene — not as a lazy default.
At the VERY END of your output, emit a hidden tag the reader NEVER sees (the displayer strips it): <!--sceneDuty: <one duty above> | attraction: none|latent|leaking|foreground-->. Set attraction=foreground ONLY when the scene is relationship-primary.

  • NEVER narrate that the lock turned ("she let him carry it" — the lock is in the LETTING itself, not in narrating that she let him).
  • SHOW the lock turning; do NOT explain it.

header: WISHCRAFT PACING — MAGIC PUNCTUATES, IT NEVER FILLS (the risk is WALLPAPER, not whimsy)
body:
Wishcraft must be RARE enough that meeting it makes a reader STOP — "who would have wished for this? what did it cost?" — never so constant it becomes wallpaper (the Harry-Potter trap: a magical candy / painting / sport every few pages until magic loses its awe). Keep the mix roughly ~70–80% ORDINARY human drama (romance, intrigue, danger, politics), ~15–20% wishcraft touching the story NATURALLY, ~5% genuine WONDER or HORROR. Magic PUNCTUATES the story; it does not fill it.
THE SACRED RULE — EVERY MAGICAL THING INVITES A QUESTION, never a shrug: not "that's neat" but "who PAID for this?", "why would anyone MAKE it?", "what happened to the one who wished for it?". Each artifact, place, creature, or phenomenon is EVIDENCE of a human decision and a sacrifice — the fossil record of thousands of wishes — so charming discoveries carry a bittersweet undercurrent and horrors a tragic inevitability, never random creepiness.
PER ~20-SCENE ISSUE (a TARGET, better under than over — never a quota to hit): ~1–2 CHARMING discoveries (a little piece of civilization built on a forgotten wish, its sacrifice quietly showing) · ~1 HORRIFYING discovery (a CONSEQUENCE, NOT necessarily a monster) · ~2–4 near-throwaway INCIDENTAL reminders that everyone lives in a wish-shaped world. Something ENORMOUS (a first-sight-of-Minas-Tirith beat — the scale of the Ascendant Run, the Fold, Fate's Favor, a Composite Wishwork masterpiece) ONLY once every FEW issues; never spend it often. INVENT each one FRESH for THIS place and people — never a stock example.
ISSUE POSITION — scene 8 of ~20: MID — a fair WINDOW for a charming discovery if one truly fits; do not force it.

LOOKBACK WINDOW: default = last 3 turns; extended = last 4 (only where explicitly named). Don't mix sizes per decision.
  BEAT BUDGET: 1 primary behavior + 1 attraction source + 1–2 targeting + 1 PC reaction + 0–1 silence + 0–1 interruption per beat. Stacked behaviors → split into consecutive beats.
  PRIORITY STACK: BEHAVIORAL > TENSION > PACING. Higher overrides lower; pacing shapes, never erases.
  TIE-BREAKER (within layer): least-used (3-turn window) → forward-motion → compressed.
  END-OF-BEAT CHECK: PROGRESSION (changed?) + VARIATION (avoided repeat?) + IMPACT (anything landed?). Fail any → rewrite.
  FAST-PATH RECOVERY: fix exactly ONE dimension (sharpen / swap / strengthen). Re-check.
  NO-OP GUARD: rewrite must materially shift PROG/VAR/IMPACT. Synonym swap / reorder / filler = no-op → discard, try different fix. Multiple consecutive no-ops → cut the beat.
  COHERENCE LOCK: no contradictions to character intent / spatial-temporal continuity / tone / prior actions / stated intent. If fix breaks coherence → reject. Coherence outranks improvement.

INTERPRETATION OVERRIDE: attraction is INTERPRETIVE, not descriptive. Risky / dominant LI behavior must feel less threatening, more charged, more confusing, more compelling — never neutral description + standard reaction.
  FAILURE: swap LI for an unattractive one — if PC reaction reads identically, scene is wrong.

BEHAVIORAL DRIFT: attraction must alter what the PC DOES, not just what she notices. After a charged beat: hesitate vs pull-away / stay vs leave / soften vs sharpen / engage vs disengage. Small, deniable, cumulative.
  FAILURE: same choices PC would make without attraction (only different inner thoughts) → texture failed.

When describing emotion, prefer physical expression over abstract summary. Express through: body movement, breath, posture, hand/eye movement, object interaction, environmental reaction.
If an emotional concept appears, precede it with a physical signal.
Allow emotion through dialogue: "You knew," she said quietly > "She felt betrayed."


ARCHETYPE_LABEL_BAN: Heart Warden, Open Vein, Spellbinder, Armored Fox, Dark Vice, Beautiful Ruin, Eternal Flame are internal labels — NEVER in prose. Express traits through behavior only.

CONCRETE_REVEAL: New story elements must reveal their significance within 2 scenes. Fact first, emotion second.

DIALOGUE_MOMENTUM: After ~3 dialogue exchanges, inject a scene state change before continuing conversation.

ESCALATION: Tension never resets to zero. Each scene deepens at least one unresolved tension.

FATE_CARD_ESCALATION: Fate Cards adjust trajectory — Confession→vulnerability, Boundary→resistance, Temptation→risk, Reversal→power flip, Silence→withheld tension.

ROMANCE_AND_BODY: Body language introduces romantic tension before dialogue confirms it. Emotional declarations must shift the relationship — no easy reciprocation.

PLAYER_CAUSALITY: Player actions produce visible scene shifts. Never acknowledge then ignore.
